units.zh: 梁書卷第三十八 列傳第三十二
units.en: Book of Liang, Volume 38, Biography 32
units.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 38, Biography 32

units.zh: 朱异 賀琛
units.en: Zhu Yi; He Chen
units.literal: Zhu Yi; He Chen

units.zh: 朱异字彥和，吳郡錢唐人也。
units.en: Zhu Yi, whose courtesy name was Yanhe, came from Qiantang in Wu Commandery.
units.literal: Zhu Yi, courtesy name Yanhe, was a native of Qiantang in Wu Commandery.

units.zh: 父巽，以義烈知名，官至齊江夏王參軍、吳平令。
units.en: His father Xun won renown for steadfast courage and rose to be an aide to Qi’s Prince of Jiangxia and magistrate of Wuping.
units.literal: His father Xun was famed for righteous valor and reached the posts of Military Aide to the Prince of Jiangxia of Qi and Magistrate of Wuping.

units.zh: 异年數歲，外祖顧歡撫之，謂异祖昭之曰：「此兒非常器，當成卿門戶。」
units.en: While Yi was still small, his maternal grandfather Gu Huan held him on his knee and told Yi’s grandfather Zhao Zhi, "This child is no common talent—he will uphold your clan."
units.literal: When Yi was only a few years old, his maternal grandfather Gu Huan dandled him and said to Yi’s grandfather Zhao Zhi: "This boy is no ordinary vessel; he will bring honor to your house."

units.zh: 年十餘歲，好羣聚蒲博，頗爲鄉黨所患。
units.en: By his teens he ran with gamblers in the lanes and became something of a trial to the township.
units.literal: At ten and more he loved gathering in crowds for gambling and was quite a nuisance to the neighborhood.

units.zh: 旣長，乃折節從師，遍治《五經》，尤明《禮》、《易》，涉獵文史，兼通雜藝，博弈書算，皆其所長。
units.en: When he matured he checked his ways, took up study under masters, and worked through the Five Classics, excelling in the Rites and the Changes while reading broadly in belles-lettres and history; he also picked up assorted skills—games, chess, writing, and calculation were alike his forte.
units.literal: Once grown, he reformed his conduct and followed teachers, studying all the Five Classics thoroughly; he was especially versed in the Rites and the Changes, ranged widely in letters and history, and mastered miscellaneous arts—go, chess, calligraphy, and reckoning were all among his strengths.

units.zh: 年二十，詣都，尚書令沈約面試之，因戲异曰：「卿年少，何乃不廉？」
units.en: At twenty he presented himself at court; Director Shen Yue tested him face to face and teased, "You are young—why so stingy?"
units.literal: At twenty he went to the capital; the Director of the Secretariat Shen Yue examined him in person and, in jest, said to Yi: "You are still young—why so ungenerous?"

units.zh: 异逡巡未達其旨。
units.en: Yi faltered, unable to catch the point of the joke.
units.literal: Yi hesitated, not yet grasping his meaning.

units.zh: 約乃曰：「天下唯有文義棋書，卿一時將去，可謂不廉也。」
units.en: Then Yue explained: "In all the realm only literary arts, chess, and calligraphy matter—and you walk off with every one at once; that is stinginess indeed."
units.literal: Yue then said: "Under heaven there are only literary arts, chess, and calligraphy—yet you carry them all off at once; one might call that ungenerous indeed."

units.zh: 其年，上書言建康宜置獄司，比廷尉。
units.en: In that same year he memorialized that Jiankang ought to establish a prison bureau modeled on the Court of Review.
units.literal: That year he submitted a memorial arguing that Jiankang should have a prison office on the model of the Court of Review.

units.zh: 敕付尚書詳議，從之。
units.en: The throne ordered the Secretariat to examine the plan in detail, and it was approved.
units.literal: An edict ordered the Secretariat to deliberate in detail, and the proposal was adopted.

units.zh: 舊制，年二十五方得釋褐。
units.en: By longstanding custom, men did not enter office until twenty-five.
units.literal: Under the old rule, one had to be twenty-five before shedding coarse dress for office.

units.zh: 時异適二十一，特敕擢爲揚州議曹從事史。
units.en: Yi was just twenty-one, yet an exceptional order promoted him to clerk in Yang Province’s council office.
units.literal: Yi was then only twenty-one, but a special edict raised him to Clerk in the Council Office of Yang Province.

units.zh: 尋有詔求異能之士，《五經》博士明山賓表薦异曰：「竊見錢唐朱异，年時尚少，德備老成。
units.en: Before long the court called for exceptional talent; Five Classics Erudite Ming Shanbin recommended Yi, writing, "I have seen Zhu Yi of Qiantang—young in years, yet already mature in conduct.
units.literal: Soon an edict sought men of outstanding ability; the Erudite of the Five Classics Ming Shanbin memorialized recommending Yi, saying: "I have observed Qiantang’s Zhu Yi—still young in years, yet complete in the virtue of age.

units.zh: 在獨無散逸之想，處暗有對賓之色，器宇弘深，神表峰峻。
units.en: In solitude he shows no wandering mind; in quiet he keeps the composure of a host receiving guests—his bearing is vast, his presence steep and bright.
units.literal: Alone he harbors no thoughts of dissipation; in seclusion he bears the bearing of one facing guests; his capacity is broad and deep, his spirit lofty and sharp.

units.zh: 金山萬丈，緣陟未登；
units.en: A golden mountain rises ten thousand feet, yet its summit is still unscaled;
units.literal: A golden mountain ten thousand feet high—one has not yet climbed its heights;

units.zh: 玉海千尋，窺映不測。
units.en: a jade ocean stretches a thousand fathoms, and no eye can plumb it.
units.literal: a jade sea a thousand fathoms deep—gaze into it and its depths cannot be measured.

units.zh: 加以珪璋新琢，錦組初構，觸響鏗鏘，值采便發。
units.en: His jade is newly polished, his brocade freshly woven—strike him and the tone rings true; set him a task and he answers on the spot.
units.literal: Add to this that his jade tablet is freshly cut and his brocade cords newly tied—strike it and the ring is clear; touch its colors and it answers at once.

units.zh: 觀其信行，非惟十室所稀，若使負重遙途，必有千里之用。」
units.en: Judge his trustworthiness and action: he is scarce even among ten households; set him to carry weight over a long road and he will go a thousand li."
units.literal: Consider his faith and conduct: they are rare not merely in one household; if you set him to bear a heavy burden on a long road, he will surely serve for a thousand li."

units.zh: 高祖召見，使說《孝經》、《周易》義，甚悅之，謂左右曰：「朱异實異。」
units.en: The Founding Emperor received him, heard him lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Book of Changes, and delighted in him, telling his attendants, "Zhu Yi is indeed exceptional."
units.literal: The Founding Emperor summoned him, had him expound the Classic of Filial Piety and the Book of Changes, was greatly pleased, and said to those beside him: "Zhu Yi is truly extraordinary."

units.zh: 後見明山賓，謂曰：「卿所舉殊得其人。」
units.en: Later, meeting Ming Shanbin, he said, "Your recommendation hit the mark."
units.literal: Later, seeing Ming Shanbin, he said: "The man you recommended is truly the right one."

units.zh: 仍召异直西省，俄兼太學博士。
units.en: He called Yi to regular duty in the Western Secretariat and shortly made him an erudite of the Imperial Academy as well.
units.literal: He then summoned Yi to the Western Secretariat on permanent duty and soon added the post of Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

units.zh: 其年，高祖自講《孝經》，使异執讀。
units.en: In that year the emperor personally expounded the Classic of Filial Piety and appointed Yi to hold the book and read.
units.literal: That year the Founding Emperor himself lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety and had Yi hold the text and read aloud.

units.zh: 遷尚書儀曹郎，入兼中書通事舍人，累遷鴻臚卿，太子右衛率，尋加員外常侍。
units.en: He rose to gentleman in the secretariat’s ceremonial office, served concurrently as a palace secretariat attendant, and climbed through chamberlain for dependencies, right commandant of the heir’s guards, and supernumerary palace attendant.
units.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Ceremonial Office of the Secretariat, entered service concurrently as Palace Secretariat Attendant, and was promoted in succession to Chamberlain for Dependencies, Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent’s Guards, and then Supernumerary Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 普通五年，大舉北伐，魏徐州刺史元法僧遣使請舉地內屬，詔有司議其虛實。
units.en: In Putong year five the court mounted a major northern campaign; Yuan Faseng, Wei governor of Xuzhou, sent envoys to offer his province in submission, and the throne ordered officials to test the offer’s sincerity.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Putong a great northern expedition was launched; Yuan Faseng, Wei governor of Xuzhou, sent envoys offering to surrender his territory and submit to the dynasty, and an edict ordered the relevant offices to judge whether the offer was genuine.

units.zh: 异曰：「自王師北討，剋獲相繼，徐州地轉削弱，咸願歸罪法僧，法僧懼禍之至，其降必非偽也。」
units.en: Yi argued: "Ever since our northern campaigns began, triumph has piled on triumph; Xuzhou weakens daily, and everyone wants to blame Faseng—so, terrified of ruin, he cannot be faking his surrender."
units.literal: Yi said: "Since our armies marched north, victories have followed one after another; the land of Xuzhou grows ever weaker, and all wish to lay the blame on Faseng. Faseng, fearing disaster, will surely not feign surrender."

units.zh: 高祖仍遣异報法僧，並敕衆軍應接，受异節度。
units.en: The emperor dispatched Yi to answer Faseng and directed the field armies to cooperate, all under Yi’s direction.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor then sent Yi to reply to Faseng and also ordered the armies to support him, placing them under Yi’s command.

units.zh: 旣至，法僧遵承朝旨，如异策焉。
units.en: On arrival Yi found Faseng obeying the court’s orders exactly as he had predicted.
units.literal: When Yi arrived, Faseng followed the court’s instructions just as Yi had foreseen.

units.zh: 中大通元年，遷散騎常侍。
units.en: In Zhongdatong year one he became palace attendant.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhongdatong he was promoted to Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 自周舍卒後，异代掌機謀，方鎮改換，朝儀國典，詔誥敕書，並兼掌之。
units.en: When Zhou She died, Yi inherited control of state planning—frontier appointments, court ritual, national statutes, and every edict and order flowed through him.
units.literal: After Zhou She died, Yi took over planning at the inner court; changes of frontier commanders, court ritual and state statutes, and all edicts, proclamations, and orders passed through his hands as well.

units.zh: 每四方表疏，當局簿領，諮詢詳斷，填委於前。
units.en: Memorials from every direction, the registers of each bureau, and files awaiting judgment and reply heaped up on his desk.
units.literal: Each memorial from the four quarters, every ledger of the responsible office, and each matter for consultation and decision piled up before him.

units.zh: 异屬辭落紙，覽事下議，縱橫敏贍，不暫停筆，頃刻之間，諸事便了。
units.en: He drafted as he scanned, glanced at a case and sent it on for debate—swift, fluent, brush never still—and within moments the stack was cleared.
units.literal: Yi would set words to paper as he read, glance at a matter and send it down for deliberation—nimble and resourceful, never pausing his brush; in the space of a moment every item was disposed of.

units.zh: 大同四年，遷右衛將軍。
units.en: In Datong 4, Yi was promoted to General of the Right Guard.
units.literal: In Datong 4, Yi was promoted to General of the Right Guard.

units.zh: 六年，异啓於儀賢堂奉述高祖《老子義》，敕許之。
units.en: In the sixth year, Yi petitioned to reverently expound Gaozu's Meaning of the Laozi in Yixian Hall, and an edict permitted it.
units.literal: In the sixth year, Yi petitioned to reverently expound Gaozu's Meaning of the Laozi in Yixian Hall, and an edict permitted it.

units.zh: 及就講，朝士及道俗聽者千餘人，爲一時之盛。
units.en: When he began the lectures, more than a thousand court officials, Daoists, and laypeople came to listen, making it a grand event of the time.
units.literal: When he began the lectures, more than a thousand court officials, Daoists, and laypeople came to listen, making it a grand event of the time.

units.zh: 時城西又開士林館以延學士，异與左丞賀琛遞日述高祖《禮記中庸義》，皇太子又召异於玄圃講《易》。
units.en: At the time, the Shilin Hall west of the city was also opened to host scholars. Yi and Left Assistant Director He Chen took turns by day expounding Gaozu's Meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean in the Book of Rites, and the crown prince also summoned Yi to Xuanpu to lecture on the Changes.
units.literal: At the time, the Shilin Hall west of the city was also opened to host scholars. Yi and Left Assistant Director He Chen took turns by day expounding Gaozu's Meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean in the Book of Rites, and the crown prince also summoned Yi to Xuanpu to lecture on the Changes.

units.zh: 八年，改加侍中。
units.en: In the eighth year, he was changed and additionally made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
units.literal: In the eighth year, he was changed and additionally made Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 太清元年，遷左衛將軍，領步兵。
units.en: In Taiqing 1, he was transferred to General of the Left Guard, concurrently Infantry Colonel.
units.literal: In Taiqing 1, he was transferred to General of the Left Guard, concurrently Infantry Colonel.

units.zh: 二年，遷中領軍，舍人如故。
units.en: In the second year, he was transferred to Central Leader of the Army, keeping his post as Secretariat Drafter as before.
units.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to Central Leader of the Army, keeping his post as Secretariat Drafter as before.

units.zh: 高祖夢中原平，舉朝稱慶，旦以語异，异對曰：「此宇內方一之征。」
units.en: The emperor dreamed the north was pacified; courtiers rejoiced. At dawn he told Yi, who answered, "It foretells the unification of the empire."
units.literal: The Founding Emperor dreamed that the Central Plains were pacified; the whole court offered congratulations. At dawn he told Yi, and Yi replied: "This is a sign that the realm will be united."

units.zh: 及侯景歸降，敕召羣臣議，尚書僕射謝舉等以爲不可，高祖欲納之，未決；
units.en: When Hou Jing came in with a surrender offer, the court was convoked to debate; Vice Director Xie Ju and others opposed acceptance, while the emperor leaned toward yes but could not settle his mind;
units.literal: When Hou Jing offered to surrender, an edict summoned the ministers to debate; Vice Director of the Secretariat Xie Ju and others held that it should not be accepted, while the Founding Emperor wished to agree but had not decided;

units.zh: 嘗夙興至武德閣，自言「我國家承平若此，今便受地，詎是事宜，脫致紛紜，悔無所及」。
units.en: one dawn he went early to Wude Pavilion and murmured, "The realm has known such peace—if we take his lands now, is that wise? Once disorder starts, regret will come too late."
units.literal: once he rose early and went to Wude Pavilion, saying to himself, "Our state has enjoyed peace like this—if we now take his territory, is it really fitting? Should turmoil follow, there will be no place for regret."

units.zh: 异探高祖微旨，應聲答曰：「聖明御宇，上應蒼玄，北土遺黎，誰不慕仰？
units.en: Reading the emperor’s mind, Yi answered immediately: "Under your sage rule, answering heaven above, every survivor in the north looks to you with longing—
units.literal: Yi divined the emperor’s hidden intent and answered at once: "Your sagely rule fills the throne, matching heaven’s dark mystery; the remnant people of the north—who does not look up in longing?

units.zh: 爲無機會，未達其心。
units.en: only lacking the chance to reach you.
units.literal: Only for lack of opportunity have they not yet reached your heart.

units.zh: 今侯景分魏國太半，輸誠送款，遠歸聖朝，豈非天誘其衷，人獎其計！
units.en: Now Hou Jing holds more than half of Wei, brings loyalty and tribute, and returns to the sacred court—is this not heaven inclining his heart and men rewarding his design?
units.literal: Now Hou Jing splits more than half of Wei and offers sincerity and tribute, returning from afar to the holy court—is this not heaven opening his breast and men praising his plan!

units.zh: 原心審事，殊有可嘉。
units.en: Weigh motive and fact together, and much deserves praise.
units.literal: Weigh his intent and examine the matter: there is much to commend.

units.zh: 今若不容，恐絕後來之望。
units.en: Reject him now and you may extinguish the hopes of all who would follow.
units.literal: If you do not accept him now, I fear you will cut off the hopes of those who come after.

units.zh: 此誠易見，願陛下無疑。」
units.en: The point is plain; I pray Your Majesty will not hesitate."
units.literal: This is easy to see; I beg Your Majesty to harbor no doubt."

units.zh: 高祖深納异言，又感前夢，遂納之。
units.en: The emperor embraced Yi’s counsel, remembered his dream, and accepted Hou Jing.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor took Yi’s words deeply to heart, was moved as well by his earlier dream, and accepted the surrender.

units.zh: 及貞陽敗沒，自魏遣使還，述魏相高澄欲更申和睦。
units.en: After Prince Zhenyang fell into Wei hands, messengers returned saying Chancellor Gao Cheng wished to restore peace.
units.literal: When Zhenyang was captured and lost, envoys returned from Wei reporting that Chancellor Gao Cheng wished to renew friendly relations.

units.zh: 敕有司定議，异又以和爲允，高祖果從之。
units.en: The throne ordered deliberation; Yi again favored peace, and the emperor agreed.
units.literal: An edict ordered the offices to decide; Yi again judged peace acceptable, and the Founding Emperor followed him.

units.zh: 其年六月，遣建康令謝挺、通直郎徐陵使北通好。
units.en: That sixth month he sent Jiankang magistrate Xie Ting and direct attendant Xu Ling north to negotiate amity.
units.literal: In the sixth month of that year he sent Xie Ting, Magistrate of Jiankang, and Xu Ling, Direct Attendant, north to treat for peace.

units.zh: 是時，侯景鎮壽春，累啓絕和，及請追使。
units.en: Hou Jing, then at Shouchun, repeatedly petitioned to sever relations and recall the mission.
units.literal: At that time Hou Jing was stationed at Shouchun and repeatedly memorialized to break off relations and to recall the envoys.

units.zh: 又致書與异，辭意甚切，异但述敕旨以報之。
units.en: He wrote to Yi as well, his tone sharp; Yi answered solely by citing the emperor’s orders.
units.literal: He also wrote to Yi in very urgent terms; Yi only relayed the wording of the edict in reply.

units.zh: 八月，景遂舉兵反，以討异爲名。
units.en: In the eighth month Hou Jing rebelled, naming his cause the punishment of Zhu Yi.
units.literal: In the eighth month Jing raised troops in revolt, taking "punishing Yi" as his slogan.

units.zh: 募兵得三千人，及景至，仍以其衆守大司馬門。
units.en: Yi mustered three thousand men and, when Hou Jing came, still held the Grand Marshal’s gate with them.
units.literal: He raised three thousand men, and when Jing arrived Yi still used that force to hold the Gate of the Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 初，景謀反，合州刺史鄱陽王範、司州刺史羊鴉仁並累有啓聞，异以景孤立寄命，必不應爾，乃謂使者：「鄱陽王遂不許國家有一客！」
units.en: Before the revolt, Prince Fan of Poyang and Governor Yang Yarén of Si had sent repeated warnings; Yi, believing Hou Jing isolated and clinging to the court’s protection, would never dare rebel, told their couriers, "The Prince of Poyang will not even let the state keep one guest!"
units.literal: Earlier, when Jing plotted rebellion, Prince of Poyang Fan, Governor of He Province, and Yang Yarén, Governor of Si Province, had repeatedly memorialized warning of it; Yi, thinking Jing isolated and dependent on the court’s mercy, would surely not act so, told the messengers: "The Prince of Poyang simply will not let the state keep a single guest!"

units.zh: 並抑而不奏，故朝廷不爲之備。
units.en: And buried their reports, so the capital was caught unprepared.
units.literal: and suppressed the memorials without forwarding them, so the court made no preparations.

units.zh: 及寇至，城內文武咸尤之。
units.en: When the enemy reached the walls, every official inside the city reproached him.
units.literal: When the invader reached the city, civil and military officials within the walls all blamed him.

units.zh: 皇太子又制《圍城賦》，其末章云：「彼高冠及厚履，並鼎食而乘肥，升紫霄之丹地，排玉殿之金扉，陳謀謨之啓沃，宣政刑之福威，四郊以之多壘，萬邦以之未綏。
units.en: The crown prince wrote the "Rhapsody on the Besieged City," whose final lines run: "They of high caps and thick soles, feasting on rich fare and riding plump horses, climb the scarlet courts of purple heaven and thrust open the golden gates of jade halls—counseling at the inner audience, wielding the blessings and terrors of law—till the suburbs bristle with ramparts and the realm knows no rest.
units.literal: The Crown Prince also composed the "Rhapsody on Besieging the City"; its closing section reads: "Those with high caps and thick shoes, all feasting richly and riding fat steeds, ascend the cinnabar ground of purple heaven and push open the golden doors of jade halls, presenting counsel at the inner court and proclaiming the blessings and terrors of government and punishment—so the four suburbs grow many ramparts and the myriad states know no peace.

units.zh: 問豺狼其何者？
units.en: Who are the wolves and jackals?
units.literal: Ask: which are the wolves and jackals?

units.zh: 訪虺蜴之爲誰？」
units.en: Who are the vipers and basilisks?"
units.literal: Inquire: who are the venomous snakes and lizards?"

units.zh: 蓋以指异。
units.en: The lines plainly targeted Yi.
units.literal: This was plainly aimed at Yi.

units.zh: 异因慚憤，發病卒，時年六十七。
units.en: Stung by shame and anger, Yi took ill and died at sixty-seven.
units.literal: Yi, shamed and enraged, fell ill and died, aged sixty-seven.

units.zh: 詔曰：「故中領軍异，器宇弘通，才力優贍，諮謀帷幄，多歷年所。
units.en: The edict read: "The late Central Commander-in-Chief Yi bore a great and open mind and ample talent; for years he counseled within the command tent.
units.literal: The edict said: "The late Central Commander-in-Chief Yi possessed a broad and penetrating capacity and abundant talent and strength; for many years he advised within the curtain of state.

units.zh: 方贊朝經，永申寄任。
units.en: He was to have upheld the court’s order and long borne our commission.
units.literal: He was just assisting the court’s institutions and would long have carried our trust.

units.zh: 奄先物化，惻悼兼懷。
units.en: Suddenly he left the world, and our sorrow is twofold.
units.literal: Suddenly he passed from among the living; our grief is doubled.

units.zh: 可贈侍中、尚書右僕射，給秘器一具。
units.en: Let him be mourned as Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, with one set of secret burial vessels.
units.literal: He may be posthumously awarded Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, with one set of secret burial vessels granted.

units.zh: 凶事所須，隨由資辦。」
units.en: All funeral needs are to be furnished as required."
units.literal: Whatever the funeral requires shall be supplied as needed."

units.zh: 舊尚書官不以爲贈，及异卒，高祖惜之，方議贈事。
units.en: Formerly secretariat posts were not granted posthumously; when Yi died the emperor grieved and debated what honor to give.
units.literal: By old custom ministerial offices were not given as posthumous titles; when Yi died the Founding Emperor regretted it and was just then debating the award.

units.zh: 左右有善异者，乃啓曰：「异忝曆雖多，然平生所懷，願得執法。」
units.en: An attendant who admired Yi submitted: "For all his long service, his lifelong wish was to wield the law."
units.literal: A courtier who favored Yi then memorialized: "Though Yi’s years of service were many, what he cherished all his life was to hold the law."

units.zh: 高祖因其宿志，特有此贈焉。
units.en: Honoring that lifelong wish, the emperor granted this exceptional title.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor, honoring his old wish, made this special grant.

units.zh: 异居權要三十餘年，善窺人主意曲，能阿諛以承上旨，故特被寵任。
units.en: For over thirty years Yi stood at the center of power, reading every nuance of the emperor’s mood, flattering and aligning with his wishes until favor became absolute.
units.literal: Yi held power for more than thirty years, skilled at reading the twists of the sovereign’s mind; he could flatter and follow the throne’s intent, and so enjoyed exceptional trust.

units.zh: 歷官自員外常侍至侍中，四官皆珥貂，自右衛率至領軍，四職並驅鹵簿，近代未之有也。
units.en: From supernumerary palace attendant through palace attendant he wore the sable at four offices; from right guard commandant to commander-in-chief he led the imperial escort at four commands—unprecedented in living memory.
units.literal: In office from Supernumerary Palace Attendant to Palace Attendant he wore the courtier’s sable at four ranks; from Right Commandant of the Guards to Commander-in-Chief he led the imperial guard procession at four posts—such a thing had not occurred in recent times.

units.zh: 异及諸子自潮溝列宅至青溪，其中有臺池翫好，每暇日與賓客遊焉。
units.en: Yi and his sons strung mansions from Chaogou to Qingxi, with gardens and pools for delight, and on leisure days entertained guests there.
units.literal: Yi and his sons had contiguous mansions from Chaogou to Qingxi, with terraces and pools for pleasure; on free days he roamed there with guests.

units.zh: 四方所饋，財貨充積。
units.en: Tribute from every quarter packed his storehouses with riches.
units.literal: Gifts from the four quarters filled his stores with wealth.

units.zh: 性吝嗇，未嘗有散施。
units.en: He was tight-fisted by nature and never gave freely.
units.literal: By nature he was miserly and never gave largesse.

units.zh: 廚下珍羞腐爛，每月常棄十數車，雖諸子別房亦不分贍。
units.en: Fine foods spoiled in his kitchens; each month he threw away ten-odd cartloads of delicacies, and would not even share them with his sons in other residences.
units.literal: Delicacies in his kitchens rotted away; every month he routinely discarded a dozen or more cartloads, and even his sons in separate households received no share.

units.zh: 所撰《禮》、《易》講疏及儀注、文集百餘篇，亂中多亡逸。
units.en: His exegeses on the Rites and Changes, ritual manuals, and collected works ran to more than a hundred chapters, most of which perished in the rebellion.
units.literal: He compiled commentaries on the Rites and the Changes, ritual regulations, and collected writings in more than a hundred chapters; most were lost in the disorders.

units.zh: 長子肅，官至國子博士；
units.en: His eldest son Su rose to erudite of the National University;
units.literal: His eldest son Su reached the post of Erudite of the National University;

units.zh: 次子閏，司徒掾。
units.en: his second son Run served as a clerk to the Minister over the Masses.
units.literal: his second son Run was a clerk to the Minister over the Masses.

units.zh: 並遇亂卒。
units.en: Both perished in the chaos.
units.literal: Both died in the upheaval.

units.zh: 賀琛，字國寶，會稽山陰人也。
units.en: He Chen, whose courtesy name was Guobao, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.
units.literal: He Chen, courtesy name Guobao, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji Commandery.

units.zh: 伯父蒨，步兵校尉，爲世碩儒。
units.en: His uncle Qian, commandant of footsoldiers, was a preeminent scholar of the time.
units.literal: His father’s elder brother Qian was Commandant of Footsoldiers and a leading scholar of the age.

units.zh: 琛幼，蒨授其經業，一聞便通義理。
units.en: As a boy Chen studied under Qian; hear a passage once and he understood it.
units.literal: When Chen was young, Qian taught him the classics; with one hearing he grasped their meaning.

units.zh: 蒨異之，常曰：「此兒當以明經致貴。」
units.en: Qian admired him and often said, "This child will win rank through the classics."
units.literal: Qian marveled at him and often said: "This boy will rise to honor through mastery of the classics."

units.zh: 蒨卒後，琛家貧，常往還諸暨，販粟以自給。
units.en: After Qian’s death the family was poor; Chen shuttled to Zhuji, buying and selling grain to live.
units.literal: After Qian died the Chen household was poor; he often traveled back and forth to Zhuji, trading grain to support himself.

units.zh: 閑則習業，尤精《三禮》。
units.en: In idle hours he kept at his books and became a master of the Three Rites.
units.literal: In his spare time he pursued his studies and was especially expert in the Three Rites.

units.zh: 初，蒨於鄉里聚徒教授，至是又依琛焉。
units.en: Qian had once taught a village school; now the pupils attached themselves to Chen.
units.literal: Earlier Qian had gathered disciples in the village to teach; now they came to Chen instead.

units.zh: 普通中，刺史臨川王辟爲祭酒從事史。
units.en: During Putong the Prince of Linchuan, as inspector, took him on as libationer and clerk.
units.literal: In the Putong era the Prince of Linchuan, as regional inspector, engaged him as Libationer and Clerk.

units.zh: 琛始出都，高祖聞其學術，召見文德殿，與語悅之，謂僕射徐勉曰：「琛殊有世業。」
units.en: On first reaching the capital Chen was summoned to Wende Hall; the emperor, pleased by their talk, told Vice Director Xu Mian, "Chen indeed inherits a scholarly house."
units.literal: When Chen first came to the capital the Founding Emperor, hearing of his learning, summoned him to Wende Hall; speaking with him, the emperor was pleased and said to Vice Director Xu Mian: "Chen truly carries on a family tradition."

units.zh: 仍補王國侍郎，俄兼太學博士，稍遷中衛參軍事、尚書通事舍人，參禮儀事。
units.en: He was made a gentleman of the prince’s establishment, then imperial academy erudite, and rose to central guard army aide and secretariat attendant, sharing in ritual matters.
units.literal: He was then appointed Gentleman of the Prince’s Kingdom, soon added as Erudite of the Imperial Academy, and gradually promoted to Army Aide in the Central Guard and Secretariat Attendant, taking part in ritual affairs.

units.zh: 累遷通直正員郎，舍人如故。
units.en: He advanced to direct attendant with regular rank while keeping his attendant post.
units.literal: He was promoted in succession to Direct Attendant with regular rank, retaining his post as Attendant.

units.zh: 又征西鄱陽王中錄事，兼尚書左丞，滿歲爲真。
units.en: He also served as recorder to the Western Expedition Prince of Poyang and concurrently left assistant director of the Secretariat, confirmed in the latter after a year.
units.literal: He was also Recorder to the Western Expedition Prince of Poyang, concurrently Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, and after a full year was confirmed in the latter post.

units.zh: 詔琛撰《新諡法》，至今施用。
units.en: The throne ordered him to draft the "New Method of Posthumous Titles," still applied today.
units.literal: An edict ordered Chen to compile the "New Method of Posthumous Titles," which is still in use today.

units.zh: 時皇太子議，大功之末，可以冠子嫁女。
units.en: Then the crown prince argued that in the final days of greater mourning one might cap one’s son or marry off one’s daughter.
units.literal: At that time the Crown Prince proposed that at the end of greater mourning one might cap a son or marry off a daughter.

units.zh: 琛駁之曰：
units.en: Chen objected in these words:
units.literal: Chen rebutted him, saying:

units.zh: 令旨以「大功之末可得冠子嫁女，不得自冠自嫁。」
units.en: The crown prince holds that "at the end of greater mourning one may crown one’s son and marry one’s daughter, but not crown oneself or marry oneself."
units.literal: The crown prince’s opinion holds that "at the end of greater mourning one may cap a son and marry off a daughter, but one may not cap oneself or marry oneself."

units.zh: 推以《記》文，竊猶致惑。
units.en: Weighing this against the Record of Rites, I remain unconvinced.
units.literal: Pushing against the text of the Record, I still find myself puzzled.

units.zh: 案嫁冠之禮，本是父之所成，無父之人，乃可自冠。
units.en: Marriage and capping are ceremonies a father performs; only the fatherless may crown themselves.
units.literal: For the rites of marriage and capping are originally what a father accomplishes; only one without a father may cap himself.

units.zh: 故稱大功小功，並以冠子嫁子爲文；
units.en: Hence in both greater and lesser mourning the phrasing is "crown the son" and "marry the daughter";
units.literal: Thus for both greater and lesser mourning the wording speaks of capping a son and marrying off a daughter;

units.zh: 非關惟得爲子，己身不得也。
units.en: it does not mean one may act for a son but not for oneself.
units.literal: it is not that one may act only for a son while oneself may not.

units.zh: 小功之末，旣得自嫁娶，而亦云「冠子娶婦」，其義益明。
units.en: At the end of lesser mourning one may already marry on one’s own account, yet the text also says "crown the son and take a wife"—which makes the sense plainer still.
units.literal: At the end of lesser mourning one may already marry oneself, yet it also says "crown the son and take a wife for him"—the meaning is clearer still.

units.zh: 故先列二服，每明冠子嫁子，結於後句，方顯自娶之義。
units.en: So the passage first names the two grades, each time specifying crowning the son and marrying the daughter, and only in the closing clause reveals the right to marry oneself.
units.literal: Therefore it first lists the two mourning grades, each explicitly stating capping the son and marrying the daughter, and in the closing line then shows the meaning of marrying oneself.

units.zh: 旣明小功自娶，卽知大功自冠矣，蓋是約言而見旨。
units.en: If lesser mourning allows self-marriage, greater mourning must allow self-capping too—the text speaks briefly but the point is clear.
units.literal: Once it is clear that in lesser mourning one may marry oneself, we know that in greater mourning one may cap oneself as well—this is a compressed statement whose intent is plain.

units.zh: 若謂緣父服大功，子服小功，小功服輕，故得爲子冠嫁，大功服重，故不得自嫁自冠者，則小功之末，非明父子服殊，不應復云「冠子嫁子」也。
units.en: If one claims that because the father is in greater mourning and the son in lesser, the lighter grade lets one crown and marry the son while the heavier forbids self-capping and self-marriage—then at the end of lesser mourning the Record would not need to stress that father and son wear different grades, nor repeat "crown the son and marry the daughter."
units.literal: If one argues that because the father wears greater mourning and the son wears lesser mourning, and lesser mourning is lighter, the son may be capped and married off while greater mourning is heavier and one may not marry or cap oneself—then at the end of lesser mourning the text would not need to say explicitly that father and son wear different grades; it should not repeat "crown the son and marry the daughter."

units.zh: 若謂小功之文言己可娶，大功之文不言己冠，故知身有大功，不得自行嘉禮，但得爲子冠嫁。
units.en: If lesser mourning allows self-marriage but greater mourning never mentions self-capping, the inference is that in greater mourning one cannot celebrate for oneself—only crown a son or marry off a daughter.
units.literal: If one holds that the text on lesser mourning says one may marry oneself, while the text on greater mourning does not say one may cap oneself, then one knows that while wearing greater mourning one may not perform joyous rites on one's own account, but may only cap and marry for one's son.

units.zh: 竊謂有服不行嘉禮，本爲吉凶不可相干。
units.en: The ban on festive rites during mourning exists so joy and grief never collide.
units.literal: I hold that wearing mourning and not performing joyous rites was originally because auspicious and inauspicious matters must not interfere with each other.

units.zh: 子雖小功之末，可得行冠嫁，猶應須父得爲其冠嫁。
units.en: A son in the final days of lesser mourning may receive cap or spouse, yet the father should still perform those rites for him.
units.literal: Although a son at the end of lesser mourning may undergo capping and marriage, still the father ought to be the one who caps and marries for him.

units.zh: 若父于大功之末可以冠子嫁子，是於吉凶禮無礙；
units.en: If a father at the end of greater mourning may crown his son and marry his daughter, joyous and mourning obligations no longer clash;
units.literal: If at the end of greater mourning a father may cap his son and marry off his daughter, then auspicious and inauspicious rites do not interfere;

units.zh: 吉凶禮無礙，豈不得自冠自嫁？
units.en: and if they do not clash, why forbid crowning or marrying on one's own account?
units.literal: If auspicious and inauspicious rites do not interfere, how can one not be allowed to cap oneself and marry oneself?

units.zh: 若自冠自嫁於事有礙，則冠子嫁子寧獨可通？
units.en: If self-capping and self-marriage are blocked, how can crowning the son or marrying the daughter alone be allowed?
units.literal: If capping oneself and marrying oneself is obstructed in principle, then how can capping the son and marrying off the daughter alone be permissible?

units.zh: 今許其冠子而塞其自冠，是琛之所惑也。
units.en: To allow crowning the son but deny self-capping—that is what puzzles Chen.
units.literal: Now to permit capping the son while blocking self-capping—that is what Chen finds puzzling.

units.zh: 又令旨推「下殤小功不可娶婦，則降服大功亦不得爲子冠嫁」。
units.en: The crown prince further argues: "If one in lower infant mourning with lesser mourning may not marry, then in reduced greater mourning one may not crown a son or marry a daughter either."
units.literal: Moreover the imperial directive infers: "If in lower infant mourning with lesser mourning one may not marry, then in reduced mourning of greater mourning one may not cap the son or marry off the daughter either."

units.zh: 伏尋此旨，若謂降服大功不可冠子嫁子，則降服小功亦不可自冠自娶，是爲凡厥降服大功小功皆不得冠娶矣。
units.en: Consider that logic: if reduced greater mourning forbids crowning or marrying for a child, reduced lesser mourning must forbid self-capping and self-marriage too—so every reduced grade, greater or lesser, would bar all cap and marriage.
units.literal: Delving into this directive: if it means that in reduced mourning of greater mourning one may not cap the son or marry the daughter, then in reduced mourning of lesser mourning one may not cap oneself or marry oneself either—in which case all reduced mourning, whether greater or lesser, would forbid capping and marriage.

units.zh: 《記》文應云降服則不可，寧得惟稱下殤？
units.en: The Record should then say simply "reduced mourning forbids it," not single out lower infant mourning alone.
units.literal: The Record ought then to say simply that reduced mourning is forbidden, rather than singling out lower infant mourning?

units.zh: 今不言降服，的舉下殤，實有其義。
units.en: Yet the text names lower infant mourning, not reduced mourning in general—and that choice is deliberate.
units.literal: Now it does not speak of reduced mourning but precisely cites lower infant mourning—there is real meaning in that.

units.zh: 夫出嫁出後，或有再降，出後之身，于本姊妹降爲大功；
units.en: Marriage out or adoption into another line can lower the grade twice; an adopted son, toward his birth sisters, wears only greater mourning;
units.literal: When a daughter is married out or a son becomes an heir in another line, there may be a second reduction; the outgoing heir's body, toward his natal sisters, is reduced to greater mourning;

units.zh: 若是大夫服士，又以尊降，則成小功。
units.en: and when a noble mourns a commoner, rank reduces the bond again to lesser mourning.
units.literal: If a grandee wears mourning for a commoner, with further reduction by rank, it becomes lesser mourning.

units.zh: 其於冠嫁，義無以異。
units.en: For capping and marriage the rule is the same.
units.literal: As for capping and marriage, there is no difference in principle.

units.zh: 所以然者，出嫁則有受我，出後則有傳重，並欲薄於此而厚於彼，此服雖降，彼服則隆。
units.en: A daughter given away is received by another house; an heir who continues another's main line owes that house the heavier bond—mourning is thinned on one side and thickened on the other.
units.literal: The reason is: marriage out means another receives you; becoming an heir elsewhere means carrying on another's main line—both intend to be light here and heavy there; though this mourning is reduced, that mourning is elevated.

units.zh: 昔實期親，雖再降猶依小功之禮，可冠可嫁。
units.en: Even when a bond that was full mourning is reduced twice, one still follows lesser mourning—and may cap or marry.
units.literal: Formerly, though the bond was full mourning, even after double reduction one still follows lesser mourning rules—capping and marriage are permitted.

units.zh: 若夫期降大功，大功降爲小功，止是一等，降殺有倫，服末嫁冠，故無有異。
units.en: When full mourning drops one grade to greater, or greater to lesser, the steps are orderly; at the end of mourning, cap and marriage are treated alike.
units.literal: If full mourning is reduced to greater mourning, and greater mourning to lesser mourning, that is only one step down each time; the reduction has order, and at the end of mourning capping and marriage are alike unexceptional.

units.zh: 惟下殤之服，特明不娶之義者，蓋緣以幼稚之故。
units.en: Only lower infant mourning expressly forbids marriage—likely because the deceased was an infant.
units.literal: Only for lower infant mourning does the text specially clarify the meaning of no marriage—probably because of infancy.

units.zh: 夭喪情深，旣無受厚佗姓，又異傳重彼宗，嫌其年稚服輕，頓成殺略，故特明不娶，以示本重之恩。
units.en: Early death stirs deep sorrow; the child neither joined another clan nor bore another line's succession—lest tender years and light dress erase the bond too fast, the text forbids marriage to preserve the original weight of kinship.
units.literal: Grief for early death runs deep; there is neither receiving honor from another surname nor carrying the main line of that clan; fearing the youth and light mourning would too sharply diminish the bond, it specially states no marriage to show the weight of the original tie.

units.zh: 是以凡厥降服，冠嫁不殊；
units.en: Hence for every reduced grade, cap and marriage are the same;
units.literal: Therefore for all reduced mourning, capping and marriage are not distinguished;

units.zh: 惟在下殤，乃明不娶。
units.en: only lower infant mourning expressly forbids marriage.
units.literal: only for lower infant mourning does it expressly forbid marriage.

units.zh: 其義若此，則不得言大功之降服，皆不可冠嫁也。
units.en: On that reading one cannot claim that every reduced greater mourning forbids cap and marriage.
units.literal: If the principle is thus, one cannot say that all reduced mourning of greater mourning forbids capping and marriage.

units.zh: 且《記》云「下殤小功」，言下殤則不得通於中上，語小功則不得兼于大功。
units.en: The Record says "lower infant mourning, lesser mourning": "lower infant" cannot cover middle or upper tiers, and "lesser mourning" cannot swallow greater mourning.
units.literal: Moreover the Record says "lower infant mourning, lesser mourning"—speaking of lower infant mourning cannot extend to middle and upper; speaking of lesser mourning cannot include greater mourning.

units.zh: 若實大小功降服皆不冠嫁，上中二殤亦不冠嫁者，《記》不得直云「下殤小功則不可」。
units.en: If every reduced greater and lesser grade, and middle and upper infant mourning too, all forbade cap and marriage, the Record could not stop at "lower infant mourning with lesser mourning is forbidden."
units.literal: If in truth all reduced mourning of greater and lesser mourning forbids capping and marriage, and middle and upper infant mourning also forbid it, the Record could not simply say "lower infant mourning with lesser mourning is forbidden."

units.zh: 恐非文意。
units.en: That, I think, is not what the text means.
units.literal: I fear that is not the text's intent.

units.zh: 此又琛之所疑也。
units.en: Here too Chen remains unconvinced.
units.literal: This too is a point Chen doubts.

units.zh: 遂從琛議。
units.en: The court adopted Chen's view.
units.literal: Thereupon Chen's opinion was followed.

units.zh: 遷員外散騎常侍。
units.en: He was promoted to supernumerary attendant of the discretionary cavalry.
units.literal: He was transferred to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Discretionary Cavalry.

units.zh: 舊尚書南坐，無貂；
units.en: By old custom ministers of the southern secretariat wore no sable;
units.literal: Formerly, when the Ministers sat facing south, they wore no sable;

units.zh: 貂自琛始也。
units.en: Chen was the first to wear it.
units.literal: the sable began with Chen.

units.zh: 頃之，遷御史中丞，參禮儀事如先。
units.en: Soon he became censor-in-chief and continued to share in ritual matters as before.
units.literal: Before long he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief, participating in ritual affairs as before.

units.zh: 琛家產旣豊，買主第爲宅，爲有司所奏，坐免官。
units.en: Chen's family was already wealthy; he purchased a former imperial mansion and was impeached and dismissed.
units.literal: Chen's household wealth was already great; he bought an imperial residence for his mansion and was impeached by the responsible officials, losing his post for it.

units.zh: 俄復爲尚書左丞，遷給事黃門侍郎，兼國子博士，未拜，改爲通直散騎常侍，領尚書左丞，並參禮儀事。
units.en: He was soon restored as left assistant director of the Secretariat, then attendant gentleman of the yellow gates and concurrent erudite of the National University—before taking the latter he was made regular-attendance adviser of the discretionary cavalry, still left assistant director and still in charge of ritual.
units.literal: Soon he was again made Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, concurrently Erudite of the National University—before taking that post he was changed to Regular-attendance Adviser of the Discretionary Cavalry, holding the post of Left Assistant Director and sharing in ritual affairs as before.

units.zh: 琛前後居職，凡郊廟諸儀，多所創定。
units.en: In every post he helped shape suburban rites and much of the court's ceremonial code.
units.literal: Throughout his successive offices, in suburban rites and all ritual matters he initiated and fixed many provisions.

units.zh: 每見高祖，與語常移晷刻，故省中爲之語曰：「上殿不下有賀雅。」
units.en: Audiences with Emperor Gaozu often ran long, and secretariat wits joked, "He who goes up to court and never comes down—that's Elegant He."
units.literal: Whenever he saw Emperor Gaozu and spoke with him, the audience often ran past the hour-mark—so within the Secretariat they had a saying: "When he goes up to the hall he does not come down—there is He the Elegant."

units.zh: 琛容止都雅，故時人呼之。
units.en: Chen's carriage was so polished that the nickname stuck.
units.literal: Chen's bearing was altogether refined, hence people called him that.

units.zh: 遷散騎常侍，參禮儀如故。
units.en: He rose to regular attendant of the discretionary cavalry and kept his ritual duties.
units.literal: He was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Discretionary Cavalry, sharing in ritual affairs as before.

units.zh: 是時，高祖任職者，皆緣飾姦諂，深害時政，琛遂啓陳事條封奏曰：
units.en: By then every man in power under Gaozu trimmed his conduct with flattery and fraud, corroding government; Chen submitted a sealed memorial, item by item, saying:
units.literal: At that time those in office under Gaozu all adorned themselves in flattery and deceit, deeply harming current policy; Chen therefore memorialized, setting forth matters item by item in a sealed memorial, saying:

units.zh: 臣荷拔擢之恩，曾不能效一職；
units.en: I have enjoyed Your Majesty's favor yet rendered no service worthy of a single post;
units.literal: Your subject has received the grace of elevation yet has never been able to serve in a single office worthily;

units.zh: 居獻納之任，又不能薦一言。
units.en: I hold a remonstrance office yet have not offered one loyal word.
units.literal: holding the post of presentation and remonstrance, yet unable to offer a single word of recommendation.

units.zh: 竊聞「慈父不愛無益之子，明君不畜無益之臣」，臣所以當食廢飧，中宵而歎息也。
units.en: I know that "a loving father keeps no useless son, a wise ruler keeps no useless minister"—and so I lose my appetite and sigh through the night.
units.literal: I have heard that "a loving father does not keep a useless son, an enlightened ruler does not keep a useless minister"—for this reason I cannot finish my meals and sigh in the middle of the night.

units.zh: 輒言時事，列之於後。
units.en: I venture to set out the times, point by point below.
units.literal: I venture to speak of current affairs, listing them below.

units.zh: 非謂謀猷，寧云啓沃。
units.en: This is not polished counsel, only an honest opening of the heart.
units.literal: I do not mean to offer strategy, but simply to open and nourish.

units.zh: 獨緘胸臆，不語妻子。
units.en: I have locked it in my breast and told neither wife nor child.
units.literal: I alone seal it in my breast and do not speak of it even to wife and children.

units.zh: 辭無粉飾，削槁則焚。
units.en: My words are unadorned; if they are rejected I will burn the draft.
units.literal: My words have no ornament; if they are cut down to bare stalk I will burn them.

units.zh: 脫得聽覽，試加省鑒。
units.en: If Your Majesty will read them, please weigh them yourself.
units.literal: If I may obtain Your Majesty's reading, please try to examine them.

units.zh: 如不允合，亮其戇愚。
units.en: If they miss the mark, bear with my blunt folly.
units.literal: If they do not meet approval, forgive my blunt foolishness.

units.zh: 其一事曰：今北邊稽服，戈甲解息，政是生聚教訓之時，而天下戶口減落，誠當今之急務。
units.en: First: the north has submitted and the armies stand down—this should be a season to gather and teach the people, yet registers shrink everywhere. Nothing is more urgent.
units.literal: The first matter says: Now the northern frontier has submitted, arms and armor are at rest—it is exactly the time to gather the people and teach them, yet household registers across the realm are falling—truly today's most urgent task.

units.zh: 雖是處雕流，而關外彌甚，郡不堪州之控總，縣不堪郡之裒削，更相呼擾，莫得治其政術，惟以應赴征斂爲事。
units.en: Depopulation touches every district, but beyond the passes it is worst: commanderies buckle under provincial oversight, counties under commandery exactions; officials harry one another and govern only by racing to meet levies.
units.literal: Though this afflicts carved inscriptions everywhere, beyond the passes it is still worse: commanderies cannot bear the provinces' overall control, counties cannot bear the commanderies' fleece and cut; they call upon one another in disturbance, unable to govern their arts of administration, only rushing levies and collections as their business.

units.zh: 百姓不能堪命，各事流移，或依於大姓，或聚于屯封，蓋不獲已而竄亡，非樂之也。
units.en: People cannot endure the burden; they flee—some to great clans, some to fortified estates—not from choice but from necessity.
units.literal: The common people cannot bear the crushing burden; each turns to flight—some rely on great clans, some cluster at estate seals—for they have no choice but to flee; they do not delight in it.

units.zh: 國家于關外賦稅蓋微，乃至年常租課，動致逋積，而民失安居，寧非牧守之過？
units.en: Taxes beyond the passes are already light, yet annual rents still pile in arrears while families lose their homes—is this not the magistrates' failure?
units.literal: The state's levies beyond the passes are in truth slight; yet year after year the regular rent falls into arrears, while the people lose settled living—is this not the fault of shepherds and magistrates?

units.zh: 東境戶口空虛，皆由使命繁數。
units.en: The east stands depopulated on the registers chiefly because envoys are too many.
units.literal: The eastern region's registered households stand empty—all because missions are numerous.

units.zh: 夫犬不夜吠，故民得安居。
units.en: When dogs need not bark at night, the people can live in peace.
units.literal: When dogs do not bark at night, the people obtain peaceful dwelling.

units.zh: 今大邦大縣，舟舸銜命者，非惟十數；
units.en: Today in large commanderies and counties a dozen boats bearing imperial orders are nothing unusual;
units.literal: Now in great commanderies and great counties those bearing orders by boat are not merely a dozen;

units.zh: 復窮幽之鄉，極遠之邑，亦皆必至。
units.en: and the remotest hamlets and farthest districts are reached without exception.
units.literal: and remote hamlets and farthest districts are also all reached without fail.

units.zh: 每有一使，屬所搔擾；
units.en: Each envoy harasses whatever lies under his charge;
units.literal: For every one envoy, the area under his authority is harassed;

units.zh: 況復煩擾積理，深爲民害。
units.en: how much more when such visits layer upon layer—the harm to the people is profound.
units.literal: how much more when harassation piles up layer upon layer—it deeply harms the people.

units.zh: 駑困邑宰，則拱手聽其漁獵；
units.en: Worn-out county magistrates fold their hands while envoys plunder;
units.literal: Mired and exhausted magistrates then fold their hands and listen while envoys fish and hunt;

units.zh: 桀黠長吏，又因之而爲貪殘。
units.en: and brutal senior officials use the chance to grow greedier still.
units.literal: brutal and cunning senior officials take the occasion to become greedy and cruel.

units.zh: 縱有廉平，郡猶掣肘。
units.en: Even an honest man finds the commandery pulling his elbows.
units.literal: Even if there were incorruptible and fair men, the commandery still would rein in their elbows.

units.zh: 故邑宰懷印，類無考績，細民棄業，流冗者多，雖年降復業之詔，屢下蠲賦之恩，而終不得反其居也。
units.en: Magistrates keep their seals but face no real review; commoners quit their trades and wanderers multiply—edicts recall them to the fields and taxes are forgiven again and again, yet they never return home.
units.literal: Thus magistrates clutching their seals mostly have no scrutinized performance; petty folk abandon their occupations and the drifting homeless are many—though year after year decrees of return to farming descend and repeated favors of tax remission are issued, in the end they cannot return to their homes.

units.zh: 其二事曰：聖主恤隱之心，納隍之念，聞之遐邇，至於翾飛蠕動，猶且度脫，況在兆庶。
units.en: Second: the sage ruler's pity for the suffering and his will to save the drowning reach the four quarters—even insects he would spare, how much more the people.
units.literal: The second matter says: The sage lord's heart of pity for the hidden, and the thought of receiving the drowning in the moat, are heard far and near—even flying insects and wriggling creatures he would still deliver—how much more the myriad people.

units.zh: 而州郡無恤民之志，故天下顒顒，惟注仰於一人，誠所謂「愛之如父母，仰之如日月，敬之如鬼神，畏之如雷霆」。
units.en: Yet provinces and commanderies show no care for the people, so the realm fixes its hope on Your Majesty alone—as the saying has it, "loving you as parents, looking up as to sun and moon, revering you as spirits, fearing you as thunder."
units.literal: Yet provinces and commanderies lack the will to comfort the people, so all under heaven look up expectantly to one man alone—truly what is called "loving him as parents, looking up to him as sun and moon, revering him as spirits, fearing him as thunder."

units.zh: 苟須應痛逗藥，豈可不治之哉？
units.en: When the body aches, medicine must follow—how can the sickness go untreated?
units.literal: If medicine must be applied where there is pain, how can one fail to treat it?

units.zh: 今天下宰守所以皆尚貪殘，罕有廉白者，良由風俗侈靡。
units.en: Today magistrates and governors are greedy and cruel, rarely honest—because extravagant custom drives them to it.
units.literal: Today all the realm's magistrates and guardians for this reason mostly prize greed and cruelty, rarely being clean and white—truly it is the custom of extravagant display that makes them so.

units.zh: 使之然也。
units.en: Luxury makes them so.
units.literal: that makes them so.

units.zh: 淫奢之弊，其事多端，粗舉二條，言其尤者。
units.en: Extravagance has many faces; I name two of the worst.
units.literal: The abuses of wanton luxury have many aspects; I roughly offer two items, speaking of the chief ones.

units.zh: 夫食方丈于前，所甘一味。
units.en: Before a table ten feet across, the tongue savors only one taste.
units.literal: Before a table ten feet square, what the palate delights in is but one flavor.

units.zh: 今之燕喜，相競誇豪，積果如山嶽，列肴同綺繡，露臺之產，不周一燕之資，而賓主之間，裁取滿腹，未及下堂，已同臭腐。
units.en: Today's feasts compete in display—fruit heaped like hills, dishes laid like brocade; a terrace garden's yield cannot pay for one banquet, yet host and guest eat only their fill and leave the rest to rot before they quit the hall.
units.literal: Today's banquets vie in boasting extravagance—fruit piled like mountains, dishes spread like brocade; the yield of a terrace garden does not suffice for one feast's cost, while between host and guest they take only a full belly—before leaving the hall it is already like rotting stench.

units.zh: 又歌姬儛女，本有品制，二八之錫，良待和戎。
units.en: Courtesans and dancers once had fixed ranks; the "two eight" maidens were reserved for pacifying barbarians.
units.literal: Again, singing girls and dancing women originally had their grades; the gift of "two eights" was truly reserved for harmonizing with the barbarians.

units.zh: 今畜妓之夫，無有等秩，雖復庶賤微人，皆盛姬薑，務在貪污，爭飾羅綺。
units.en: Today men who keep women observe no rank—even the humblest pack their houses with concubines, greedy for graft, vying in silk and finery.
units.literal: Today men who keep courtesans have no rank distinction—even humble and lowly men all fill their quarters with beauties, striving in corruption, competing to adorn with silk.

units.zh: 故爲吏牧民者，競爲剝削，雖致貲巨億，罷歸之日，不支數年，便已消散。
units.en: Officials who should shepherd the people race to strip them; though they amass tens of millions, a few years after leaving office the fortune is gone.
units.literal: Therefore those who as officials shepherd the people compete in stripping and cutting; though they amass wealth in the hundreds of millions, by the day they leave office, within a few years it is already dissipated.

units.zh: 蓋由宴醑所費，旣破數家之產；
units.en: Banquets alone can ruin several families' worth;
units.literal: For the cost of banquets and feasts has already ruined several households' property;

units.zh: 歌謠之具，必俟千金之資。
units.en: and song and dance demand capital of a thousand gold.
units.literal: the equipment for songs must wait on capital of a thousand gold.

units.zh: 所費事等丘山，爲歡止在俄頃。
units.en: Spending mounts like hills; pleasure lasts a breath.
units.literal: The outlay equals hills and mountains; the pleasure lasts only an instant.

units.zh: 乃更追恨向所取之少，今所費之多。
units.en: Then they regret having taken too little before and spending too much now.
units.literal: Then they further regret that what they took before was little and what they spend now is much.

units.zh: 如復傅翼，增其搏噬，一何悖哉！
units.en: Give them wings again and they tear all the harder—how perverse!
units.literal: If they are given wings again, to increase their tearing and devouring—how perverse!

units.zh: 其餘淫侈，著之凡百，習以成俗，日見滋甚，欲使人守廉隅，吏尚清白，安可得邪！
units.en: Other luxuries fill a hundred lists; habit deepens daily—how can we ask men to stay honest and officials to stay clean?
units.literal: The rest of wanton excess is written in a hundred particulars; habit becomes custom and daily grows worse—wishing men to keep clean corners and officials to honor whiteness, how can it be obtained!

units.zh: 今誠宜嚴爲禁制，道之以節儉，貶黜雕飾，糾奏浮華，使衆皆知，變其耳目，改其好惡。
units.en: Impose stern bans, teach frugality, demote ornament, impeach showy waste, until all see it and change what they desire.
units.literal: Now one should truly impose stern prohibitions, guide them with frugality, demote carved ornament, memorialize and impeach floating display, so that all know it and change what their eyes and ears take in, change what they love and hate.

units.zh: 夫失節之嗟，亦民所自患，正恥不及羣，故勉強而爲之，苟力所不至，還受其弊矣。
units.en: People too regret excess—they only fear falling behind the crowd and force themselves on; when they cannot keep up, they still bear the cost.
units.literal: The sigh at loss of restraint is also what the people themselves worry over—they are just ashamed not to match the crowd, so they force themselves to do it; if their strength does not reach, they still suffer the harm.

units.zh: 今若厘其風而正其失，易於反掌。
units.en: Correct the wind and the fault rights itself—easier than turning the hand.
units.literal: Now if one corrects the wind and rights the faults, it is easier than turning the palm.

units.zh: 夫論至治者，必以淳素爲先，正雕流之弊，莫有過儉樸者也。
units.en: Supreme rule begins in plain simplicity; to cure ornamental excess nothing beats thrift.
units.literal: In discussing supreme governance one must take plain simplicity first; in correcting the abuses of carved display nothing surpasses plain frugality.

units.zh: 其三事曰：聖躬荷負蒼生以爲任，弘濟四海以爲心，不憚胼胝之勞，不辭臒瘦之苦，豈止日昃忘饑，夜分廢寢。
units.en: Third: Your Majesty bears the people's weight and takes the four seas to heart, unafraid of toil that callouses hand and foot or hardship that wastes the flesh—forgetting hunger as the sun sets and sleep at midnight.
units.literal: The third matter says: The sacred person bears the burden of the dark-haired people as his charge, takes succoring the four seas as his heart, does not shrink from the labor of calloused hands and feet, does not decline the suffering of emaciation—how much more forgetting hunger as the sun declines and abandoning sleep at midnight.

units.zh: 至於百司，莫不奏事，上息責下之嫌，下無逼上之咎，斯實道邁百王，事超千載。
units.en: Every office may memorialize; above, no blame for pressing down, below, no fault for pressing up—a government surpassing a hundred kings.
units.literal: As for the hundred offices, none fail to memorialize; above rests the blame of pressing down, below there is no fault of pressing up—truly the Way surpasses a hundred kings, affairs exceed a thousand ages.

units.zh: 但鬥筲之人，藻棁之子，旣得伏奏帷扆，便欲詭競求進，不說國之大體。
units.en: Yet petty men, once they may speak behind the curtain, scheme for promotion and never speak for the realm's whole design.
units.literal: But petty-vessel men, chopstick-sized talents, once allowed to memorialize behind the curtain, at once wish to compete deviously for advancement, not speaking of the state's great structure.

units.zh: 不知當一官，處一職，貴使理其紊亂，匡其不及，心在明恕，事乃平章。
units.en: They forget that each post exists to set disorder right and mend what is lacking—with a heart of clarity and forbearance, affairs find their balance.
units.literal: They do not know that holding one office and filling one post means it is noble to put order to its disorder and remedy its shortfalls—the heart dwelling in clear forbearance, affairs then balanced and measured.

units.zh: 但務吹毛求疵，擘肌分理，運挈瓶之智，徼分外之求，以深刻爲能，以繩逐爲務，跡雖似於奉公，事更成其威福。
units.en: They split hairs, split hairs again, wield petty cleverness, grasp beyond their share, prize harshness and chase by the letter—seeming dutiful while building private power.
units.literal: They only pursue splitting hairs for flaws, splitting muscle to distinguish principle, wielding the wisdom of carrying a bottle, seeking reward beyond their portion, taking severity as ability and driving by the cord as their task—traces seem to serve the public, but affairs more build their authority and blessings.

units.zh: 犯罪者多，巧避滋甚，曠官廢職，長弊增姦，實由於此。
units.en: Crime multiplies, evasion grows clever, posts empty and duties rot—long corruption and fresh treachery spring from this.
units.literal: The criminal are many, clever evasion grows worse, offices lie vacant and duties abandoned, long abuses and mounting treachery—truly spring from this.

units.zh: 今誠願責其公平之效，黜其讒愚之心，則下安上謐，無僥倖之患矣。
units.en: Demand fair results, purge slanderous hearts—then the lower ranks rest, the throne is secure, and lucky scheming ends.
units.literal: Now one truly ought to demand the effect of their fairness, dismiss their slanderous foolish hearts—then below is settled and above is quiet, without the worry of lucky chance.

units.zh: 其四事曰：自征伐北境，帑藏空虛。
units.en: Fourth: northern campaigns have emptied the treasury.
units.literal: The fourth matter says: From campaigns on the northern frontier, the treasury stores stand empty.

units.zh: 今天下無事，而猶日不暇給者，良有以也。
units.en: The realm is at peace, yet you have no leisure day by day—and there is reason.
units.literal: Today the realm is without affairs, yet there is still no leisure day after day—there is good reason.

units.zh: 夫國弊則省其事而息其費，事省則養民，費息則財聚，止五年之中，尚於無事，必能使國豊民阜。
units.en: When the state is strained, cut tasks and spending; fewer tasks nurture the people, less spending piles wealth—in five years of peace the realm can grow rich.
units.literal: When the state is exhausted, reduce its affairs and rest its expenditures; when affairs are reduced the people are nurtured, when expenditures rest wealth gathers—in within five years, while still without affairs, one can surely make the state rich and the people prosperous.

units.zh: 若積以歲月，斯乃范蠡滅吳之術，管仲霸齊之由。
units.en: Sustained over years, this is how Fan Li destroyed Wu and Guan Zhong made Qi hegemon.
units.literal: If this accumulates over months and years, this is the method by which Fan Li destroyed Wu, the reason Guan Zhong made Qi hegemon.

units.zh: 今應內省職掌，各檢其所部。
units.en: Examine each office inwardly; let every department audit its own charge.
units.literal: Now one ought inwardly to examine offices' charge, each inspecting what their department does.

units.zh: 凡京師治、署、邸、肆應所爲，或十條宜省其五，或三條宜除其一；
units.en: In the capital—bureaus, offices, lodges, markets—of ten duties cut five, or of three cut one;
units.literal: As for all in the capital—administration, offices, lodges, markets—that should be done, perhaps of ten items five ought to be cut, or of three items one ought to be removed;

units.zh: 及國容、戎備，在昔應多，在今宜少。
units.en: state ceremony and armaments once needed to be many; today they should be few.
units.literal: and state display and military preparedness—in the past should have been many, today ought to be few.

units.zh: 雖于後應多，卽事未須，皆悉減省。
units.en: What future need may bring can wait; what present need does not require—cut it all.
units.literal: Though afterward more may be needed, what the affair now does not require—all alike reduce and cut.

units.zh: 應四方屯、傳、邸、治，或舊有，或無益，或妨民，有所宜除，除之；
units.en: Throughout the realm—garrisons, relays, lodges, offices—whether obsolete, useless, or harmful—abolish what should be abolished;
units.literal: All around the four quarters—garrison posts, relay stations, lodges, administrations—whether old-established, or useless, or harming the people—what should be removed, remove it;

units.zh: 有所宜減，減之。
units.en: trim what should be trimmed.
units.literal: what should be reduced, reduce it.

units.zh: 凡厥興造，凡厥費財，有非急者，有役民者；
units.en: Every project, every outlay of treasure—not urgent, or pressing the people into labor;
units.literal: All construction, all expenditure of wealth—if not urgent, if conscripting the people;

units.zh: 又凡厥討召，凡厥徵求，雖關國計，權其事宜，皆須息費休民。
units.en: Every requisition and levy, however vital to state finance, must be judged on its merits and made to spare the treasury and spare the people.
units.literal: Further, all summons and all levies—even when they touch the state accounts—must be weighed for fitness; all alike must rest spending and rest the people.

units.zh: 不息費，則無以聚財；
units.en: Unless spending is curbed, wealth cannot accumulate;
units.literal: Without resting expenditure, there is no way to gather wealth;

units.zh: 不休民，則無以聚力。
units.en: unless the people are given rest, their strength cannot be gathered.
units.literal: without resting the people, there is no way to gather strength.

units.zh: 故蓄其財者，所以大用之也；
units.en: Wealth is hoarded so it may be spent greatly;
units.literal: Thus to store wealth is precisely for great use;

units.zh: 息其民者，所以大役之也。
units.en: the people are rested so they may bear great toil.
units.literal: to rest the people is precisely for great labor.

units.zh: 若言小事不足害財，則終年不息矣；
units.en: Call waste trivial and spending never stops for a year;
units.literal: If one says small matters cannot harm wealth, then spending never rests the whole year long;

units.zh: 以小役不足妨民，則終年不止矣。
units.en: call corvée slight and conscription never ends for a year.
units.literal: if one says small corvées cannot hinder the people, then labor never stops the whole year long.

units.zh: 擾其民而欲求生聚殷阜，不可得矣。
units.en: Harass the people and expect them to multiply and prosper—that cannot be done.
units.literal: Harass the people yet wish for growth, gathering, and abundance—this cannot be obtained.

units.zh: 耗其財而務賦斂繁興，則姦詐盜竊彌生，是弊不息而其民不可使也，則難可以語富強而圖遠大矣。
units.en: Drain the treasury while heaping up taxes, and deceit and theft flourish; abuses never end and the people cannot be commanded—then there is no talking of power or far-reaching aims.
units.literal: Exhaust wealth yet pursue frequent levies, and fraud and theft multiply; evils never cease and the people cannot be employed—then it is hard to speak of wealth and strength or plan for the distant and great.

units.zh: 自普通以來，二十餘年，刑役薦起，民力雕流。
units.en: For more than twenty years since Putong, penal labor and corvée have surged without pause, and popular strength has been worn to nothing.
units.literal: Since the Putong era, for twenty-odd years, punishments and corvée have risen again and again, and the people's strength has been carved away and scattered.

units.zh: 今魏氏和親，疆埸無警，若不及於此時大息四民，使之生聚，減省國費，令府庫蓄積，一旦異境有虞，關河可掃，則國弊民疲，安能振其遠略？
units.en: The Northern Wei are reconciled and the borders are quiet. Fail now to give the people real rest, let them multiply, cut state expense, and stock the coffers, and when a neighbor turns hostile and the frontier must be held, the realm will already be hollow and the people exhausted—what grand design can you then pursue?
units.literal: Now the Wei have made peace and the marches are unalarmed; if we do not at this time greatly rest the four classes of people, let them grow and gather, reduce state costs, and fill the treasuries—once another realm grows wary and the passes must be swept clean—then with the state spent and the people weary, how can we rouse a distant strategy?

units.zh: 事至方圖，知不及矣。
units.en: Wait until crisis comes to plan, and you will find you are already too late.
units.literal: To plan only when the affair has arrived is to know that one will be too late.

units.zh: 書奏，高祖大怒，召主書於前，口授敕責琛曰：
units.en: The memorial was read; Gaozu flew into a rage, called the chief clerk to his side, and dictated a rebuke to Chen:
units.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Gaozu was greatly angered; he summoned the chief clerk before him and orally dictated an edict rebuking Chen, saying:

units.zh: 謇謇有聞，殊稱所期。
units.en: So your bold reputation precedes you—exactly as we anticipated.
units.literal: Your outspoken repute has reached us—quite what we expected.

units.zh: 但朕有天下四十餘年，公車讜言，見聞聽覽，所陳之事，與卿不異，常欲承用，無替懷抱，每苦倥傯，更增惛惑。
units.en: Yet I have ruled more than forty years. Memorials from the remonstrance office, everything brought to my ears—your complaints are nothing new. I have long meant to act on them and hold to that resolve, but am crushed by daily urgency and only grow more bewildered.
units.literal: But I have held the realm for forty-odd years; remonstrances from the carriage of petition, all that has reached my hearing and sight—the matters you state do not differ. I have often wished to adopt them and not betray my intent, yet am tormented by pressing affairs and grow only the more confused.

units.zh: 卿珥貂紆組，博問洽聞，不宜同於郤茸，止取名字，宣之行路。
units.en: You bear high rank and wide learning. You should not be like Xi Rong, collecting a reputation and peddling it in the streets.
units.literal: You wear the court insignia and gird the ribbons of office, with broad learning and wide hearing—you should not be like Xi Rong, taking only a name and proclaiming it on the road.

units.zh: 言「我能上事，明言得失，恨朝廷之不能用」。
units.en: Boasting, "I can remonstrate and lay bare what is right and wrong, and I resent that the court will not heed me."
units.literal: Saying, "I can submit affairs and speak clearly of gain and loss, and I resent that the court cannot use me."

units.zh: 或誦《離騷》「蕩蕩其無人，遂不禦乎千里」。
units.en: Or quoting the "Li Sao": "Far and wide, no true man—so the chariot will not travel a thousand li."
units.literal: Or reciting from the "Encountering Sorrow": "Vast and empty—no one there; so he will not drive a thousand li."

units.zh: 或誦《老子》「知我者希，則我貴矣」。
units.en: Or quoting the Laozi: "Few know me, and therefore I am honored."
units.literal: Or reciting from the Laozi: "Those who know me are few, and so I am prized."

units.zh: 如是獻替，莫不能言，正旦虎樽，皆其人也。
units.en: Such counsel is cheap; everyone can mouth it. The tiger goblet at New Year—that whole crowd.
units.literal: Such remonstrance and replacement—everyone can talk; the New Year tiger goblet—the lot of them.

units.zh: 卿可分別言事，啓乃心，沃朕心。
units.en: Name your charges one by one. Open your heart and refresh mine.
units.literal: You should speak of affairs item by item, open your heart, and water my heart.

units.zh: 卿云「今北邊稽服，政是生聚教訓之時，而民失安居，牧守之過」。
units.en: You wrote: "The north has submitted. This should be a time to let the people settle and thrive, yet they cannot live in peace—that is the fault of local officials."
units.literal: You say, "Now the north submits—this is precisely the time to gather and teach the people, yet they lose peaceful dwelling; the fault lies with the governors."

units.zh: 朕無則哲之知，觸向多弊，四聰不開，四明不達，內省責躬，無處逃咎。
units.en: I am no sage of discernment. I stumble into wrong after wrong. My ears and eyes do not reach everywhere. I blame only myself and cannot escape that blame.
units.literal: I lack knowing discernment; I touch on many abuses; the four hearers are unopened and the four seeers unreached—inwardly I examine and blame myself, with nowhere to flee guilt.

units.zh: 堯爲聖主，四凶在朝；
units.en: Yao was a sage, and still the Four Evils sat in court;
units.literal: Yao was a sage lord, yet the four villains were in court;

units.zh: 況乎朕也，能無惡人？
units.en: how then can I, of all men, have none?
units.literal: how much more I—can there be no wicked men?

units.zh: 但大澤之中，有龍有蛇，縱不盡善，不容皆惡。
units.en: A great marsh holds dragons and snakes alike. Not every officer is worthy, but not every one is corrupt.
units.literal: But in a great marsh there are dragons and snakes; though not all are good, not all can be wicked.

units.zh: 卿可分明顯出：某刺史橫暴，某太守貪殘，某官長凶虐；
units.en: Name them plainly: which governor is brutal, which prefect greedy and cruel, which magistrate savage;
units.literal: You may clearly name them: such-and-such a governor is violent, such-and-such a prefect greedy and cruel, such-and-such a chief brutal;

units.zh: 尚書、蘭臺，主書、舍人，某人姦猾，某人取與，明言其事，得以黜陟。
units.en: which minister, which Orchid Terrace clerk, which recorder or attendant is crooked or on the take. State the facts and they can be promoted or removed.
units.literal: which minister or Orchid Terrace clerk, which chief clerk or attendant, is crafty, which takes bribes—state the matter clearly so dismissal and promotion may follow.

units.zh: 向令舜但聽公車上書，四凶終自不知，堯亦永爲暗主。
units.en: If Shun had listened only to anonymous memorials, the Four Evils would never have been exposed and Yao would have remained a blind ruler forever.
units.literal: Had Shun only listened to memorials on the carriage of remonstrance, the four villains would never have been known, and Yao would forever have been a dim ruler.

units.zh: 卿又云「東境戶口空虛，良由使命繁多」，但未知此是何使？
units.en: You also say, "The east is depopulated because envoys are too many." Which envoys do you mean?
units.literal: You also say, "The eastern marches' households are empty, truly because missions are numerous"—but which missions are these?

units.zh: 卿云「駑困邑宰，則拱手聽其漁獵；
units.en: You say, "Weak magistrates can only stand by while others plunder;
units.literal: You say, "When incompetent district chiefs are worn down, they fold their hands while others fish and hunt;

units.zh: 桀黠長吏，又因之而爲貪殘」，並何姓名？
units.en: and crafty senior officials use the chance to grow greedier still." Who are they? Name them.
units.literal: "crafty senior officials further use this to be greedy and cruel"—what are their names?

units.zh: 廉平掣肘，復是何人？
units.en: And who are the upright officials being blocked?
units.literal: Who are the honest and fair yet hamstrung?

units.zh: 朝廷思賢，有如饑渴，廉平掣肘，實爲異事。
units.en: The throne seeks worthy men as a thirsty man seeks water. That the honest should be obstructed would be extraordinary.
units.literal: The court thirsts for the worthy as for hunger and thirst—honest men hamstrung is truly a strange thing.

units.zh: 宜速條聞，當更擢用。
units.en: List them at once. We will promote them without delay.
units.literal: Quickly itemize and report; they shall be promoted and employed anew.

units.zh: 凡所遣使，多由民訟，或復軍糧，諸所飆急，蓋不獲已而遣之。
units.en: Most missions answer lawsuits or move army grain. Urgent business leaves little choice but to send men.
units.literal: Most envoys sent are for the people's lawsuits, or again for army grain; urgencies everywhere—mostly they are sent with no choice.

units.zh: 若不遣使，天下枉直云何綜理？
units.en: Without envoys, how is justice to be done across the land?
units.literal: If envoys are not sent, how are right and wrong across the realm to be sorted?

units.zh: 事實云何濟辦？
units.en: How is real business to get done?
units.literal: How are facts to be accomplished?

units.zh: 惡人日滋，善人日蔽，欲求安臥，其可得乎！
units.en: Villains multiply by the day while the good are shut out. Do you imagine the realm can then rest easy?
units.literal: Wicked men daily multiply, good men daily eclipsed—wish to lie at ease: can this be obtained?

units.zh: 不遣使而得事理，此乃佳事。
units.en: To govern without envoys and still set everything right—that would be splendid.
units.literal: Not to send envoys yet gain orderly affairs—this would be excellent.

units.zh: 無足而行，無翼而飛，能到在所；
units.en: Feet that need not walk, wings that need not beat, yet arrival everywhere;
units.literal: To walk without feet, fly without wings, and reach wherever needed;

units.zh: 不威而伏，豈不幸甚。
units.en: obedience without coercion—what could be more fortunate?
units.literal: to submit without awe—would that not be greatly fortunate.

units.zh: 卿旣言之，應有深見，宜陳秘術，不可懷寶迷邦。
units.en: You have raised the matter, so you must know the remedy. Reveal your secret art. Do not hide wisdom and leave the realm in the dark.
units.literal: Since you have spoken thus, you must have deep insight; proclaim the secret method—do not hoard treasure and mislead the state.

units.zh: 卿又云：守宰貪殘，皆由滋味過度。
units.en: You also say, "Local greed and cruelty all come from extravagant food."
units.literal: You also say: "Governors' greed and cruelty all come from excessive delicacies."

units.zh: 貪殘糜費，已如前答。
units.en: On greed, cruelty, and waste I have already replied.
units.literal: Greed, cruelty, and wasteful spending—I have already answered as before.

units.zh: 漢文雖愛露臺之產，鄧通之錢布於天下，以此而治，朕無愧焉。
units.en: Han Wendi loved his terrace garden and Deng Tong's wealth filled the realm. I rule no worse and feel no shame.
units.literal: Han Wendi though he loved the terrace crop, Deng Tong's coin spread through the realm—with such governance I have no shame.

units.zh: 若以下民飲食過差，亦復不然。
units.en: Nor is it true that commoners eat beyond their station.
units.literal: As for common people's food overstepping bounds—that too is not so.

units.zh: 天監之初，思之已甚。
units.en: I considered this carefully at the beginning of Tianjian.
units.literal: At the start of Tianjian I thought on this deeply.

units.zh: 其勤力營產，則無不富饒；
units.en: Those who work hard prosper;
units.literal: Those who labor to build property are without exception rich;

units.zh: 惰游緩事，則家業貧窶。
units.en: the idle and careless grow poor.
units.literal: the idle and slack in affairs end in poverty.

units.zh: 勤修產業，以營盤案，自己營之，自己食之，何損於天下？
units.en: A man who builds his estate and eats what he earns—how does that harm the realm?
units.literal: Diligently manage property and set the table—oneself earn it, oneself eat it: what harm to the realm?

units.zh: 無賴子弟，惰營產業，致於貧窶，無可施設，此何益於天下？
units.en: Wastrels who neglect their fields end penniless and useless—what good is that to the realm?
units.literal: Good-for-nothing sons who idly neglect property end in poverty with nothing to deploy—what benefit to the realm?

units.zh: 且又意雖曰同富，富有不同：慳而富者，終不能設；
units.en: You speak as if all wealth were the same, but it is not. The miser may be rich yet can do nothing with it;
units.literal: And though one may speak of "equal wealth," wealth differs: the stingy rich can never deploy;

units.zh: 奢而富者，于事何損？
units.en: the spendthrift rich—what injury do they do the state?
units.literal: the lavish rich—what harm to affairs?

units.zh: 若使朝廷緩其刑，此事終不可斷；
units.en: Relax the law and excess will never end;
units.literal: If the court eases punishments, this can never be ended;

units.zh: 若急其制，則曲屋密房之中，云何可知？
units.en: tighten it and who can see what happens behind closed doors?
units.literal: if it tightens regulation, then inside curved chambers and hidden rooms—how can one know?

units.zh: 若家家搜檢，其細已甚，欲使吏不呼門，其可得乎？
units.en: Search every home and the scrutiny becomes unbearable. You want officials never to knock on a door—is that possible?
units.literal: If every house is searched, the minutiae become extreme—wish clerks never to knock at doors: can this be obtained?

units.zh: 更相恐脅，以求財帛，足長禍萌，無益治道。
units.en: Men threatening one another for money only breed worse trouble. That is no way to govern.
units.literal: Mutual intimidation to extract coin only lengthens the sprouts of disaster and benefits governance not at all.

units.zh: 若以此指朝廷，我無此事。
units.en: If you mean the court by this, I know nothing of it.
units.literal: If by this you mean the court—I have no such matter.

units.zh: 昔之牲牢，久不宰殺，朝中會同，菜蔬而已，意粗得奢約之節。
units.en: For years we ceased slaughtering for sacrifice. Court feasts were vegetables only. I thought I had found a fair balance of frugality and dignity.
units.literal: Formerly sacrificial beasts went long unslaughtered; court gatherings had only vegetables—I roughly grasped the measure of splendor and thrift.

units.zh: 若復減此，必有《蟋蟀》之譏。
units.en: Cut more and you will invite the reproach of the "Cricket."
units.literal: If this is reduced further, there will surely be the reproach of the "Cricket."

units.zh: 若以爲功德事者，皆是園中之所產育。
units.en: If you mean Buddhist merit works, their food comes from the palace gardens.
units.literal: If you think merit affairs—all are bred in the imperial gardens.

units.zh: 功德之事，亦無多費，變一瓜爲數十種，食一菜爲數十味，不變瓜菜，亦無多種，以變故多，何損於事，亦豪芥不關國家。
