units.en: Even merit feasts cost little. One melon becomes a dozen dishes, one vegetable a dozen flavors—yet without artifice there are few kinds. What harm is there in variety? It does not touch the state at all.
units.literal: Merit affairs also cost little: one melon into dozens of kinds, one dish into dozens of flavors; without changing melon or vegetable there are not many kinds—because of variety, what harm to affairs? It touches the state not in the least.

units.zh: 如得財如法而用，此不愧乎人。
units.en: Wealth lawfully gained and lawfully spent is nothing to be ashamed of.
units.literal: To obtain wealth and use it lawfully—this is no shame before men.

units.zh: 我自除公宴，不食國家之食，多歷年稔，乃至宮人，亦不食國家之食，積累歲月。
units.en: Apart from state banquets I have not eaten public rations for many years, and even the palace women have gone without them for a long time.
units.literal: I myself, apart from public feasts, do not eat the state's food—many years; even palace women do not eat state food—months piled up.

units.zh: 凡所營造，不關材官，及以國匠，皆資雇借，以成其事。
units.en: Every building project avoids the materials bureau and state craftsmen. I hire labor and pay for the work myself.
units.literal: All construction does not involve the materials office or state artisans—all is hired on loan to complete the work.

units.zh: 近之得財，頗有方便，民得其利，國得其利，我得其利，營諸功德。
units.en: Money lately raised has served everyone: the people profit, the state profits, I profit, and merit works are funded.
units.literal: Recent income has had convenient paths—the people gain, the state gains, I gain, and merit works are built.

units.zh: 或以卿之心度我之心，故不能得知。
units.en: Perhaps you judge me by yourself, and that is why you do not understand.
units.literal: Perhaps you measure my heart by your heart and therefore cannot know.

units.zh: 所得財用，暴於天下，不得曲辭辯論。
units.en: What I receive is open to the world. Do not argue in evasions.
units.literal: Income obtained is displayed to the realm—no twisting words in debate.

units.zh: 卿又云女妓越濫，此有司之責，雖然，亦有不同：貴者多畜妓樂，至於勳附若兩掖，亦復不聞家有二八，多畜女妓者。
units.en: You also complain that courtesans are too many. That is the censors' business, though the cases differ. The great mostly keep musicians, but even meritorious lords and the two palace wings—one seldom hears of a household keeping "two-eight" girls or hoarding courtesans.
units.literal: You also say female entertainers overflow—this is the responsible officials' duty; still there are differences: the noble mostly keep music girls, but even merit lords and the two flanks—one does not hear of households with "two-eight," or of many keeping female entertainers.

units.zh: 此並宜具言其人，當令有司振其霜豪。
units.en: Name every offender. Let the responsible offices strip away their arrogance.
units.literal: These should all be named; let the offices shake off their frost and pride.

units.zh: 卿又云：「乃追恨所取爲少，如復傅翼，增其搏噬，一何悖哉。」
units.en: You also wrote: "They regret having taken too little, and if given wings again they tear all the harder—how perverse!"
units.literal: You also say: "Yet they regret what they took was little; if given wings again, increasing their tearing and devouring—how perverse!"

units.zh: 勇怯不同，貪廉各用，勇者可使進取，怯者可使守城，貪者可使捍禦，廉者可使牧民。
units.en: Courage and cowardice are not the same, nor are greed and integrity. Use the brave for advance, the timid for defense, the greedy for the border, the honest for civil rule.
units.literal: Bravery and timidity differ; greed and integrity each have their use—the brave may be sent to attack, the timid to hold cities, the greedy to defend the frontier, the upright to rule the people.

units.zh: 向使叔齊守于西河，豈能濟事？
units.en: If Shu Qi alone had held the western river, would anything have been accomplished?
units.literal: Had Shu Qi alone guarded the western river, could the affair have succeeded?

units.zh: 吳起育民，必無成功。
units.en: If Wu Qi had only nurtured the people, he would never have succeeded.
units.literal: Wu Qi nurturing the people would surely have had no success.

units.zh: 若使吳起而不重用，則西河之功廢。
units.en: Had Wu Qi not been used as he deserved, the western river would never have been won.
units.literal: If Wu Qi had not been heavily employed, the achievement at the western river would have been wasted.

units.zh: 今之文武，亦復如此。
units.en: The same is true of civil and military men today.
units.literal: Today's civil and military officers are likewise.

units.zh: 取其搏噬之用，不能得不重更任，彼亦非爲朝廷爲之傅翼。
units.en: Use their predatory talents and you cannot avoid employing them heavily again. The court did not give them wings so they could prey harder.
units.literal: Take their tearing and devouring use—they cannot but be heavily employed again; the court did not give them wings for that purpose.

units.zh: 卿以朝廷爲悖，乃自甘之，當思致悖所以。
units.en: You call the court perverse yet still serve it willingly. Ask yourself what makes it perverse.
units.literal: You call the court perverse yet willingly serve it—you should consider what makes perversity.

units.zh: 卿云「宜導之以節儉」。
units.en: You say, "They should be guided by frugality."
units.literal: You say, "One should guide them with thrift."

units.zh: 又云「至治者必以淳素爲先」。
units.en: And, "Perfect government begins in plain simplicity."
units.literal: And, "Supreme rule must take plain simplicity first."

units.zh: 此言大善。
units.en: That is well said.
units.literal: These words are very fine.

units.zh: 夫子言「其身正，不令而行；
units.en: Confucius said, "When the ruler's person is upright, things are done though he does not command;
units.literal: The Master said, "If his person is upright, without being ordered it is done;

units.zh: 其身不正，雖令不從」。
units.en: when his person is not upright, they will not obey though he commands."
units.literal: if his person is not upright, though ordered they do not follow."

units.zh: 朕絕房室三十餘年，無有淫佚。
units.en: I have kept no harem for more than thirty years and have known no debauchery.
units.literal: I have cut off the inner chambers for thirty-odd years—no licentiousness.

units.zh: 朕頗自計，不與女人同屋而寢，亦三十餘年。
units.en: By my own reckoning I have not slept in the same room with a woman for more than thirty years.
units.literal: I count myself: not sleeping in the same room with women—also thirty-odd years.

units.zh: 至於居處不過一床之地，雕飾之物不入于宮，此亦人所共知。
units.en: My living space is no larger than a bed. Ornament does not enter the palace. Everyone knows this.
units.literal: My dwelling is no more than one bed's space; carved ornament never enters the palace—this too all know.

units.zh: 受生不飲酒，受生不好音聲，所以朝中曲宴，未嘗奏樂，此羣賢之所觀見。
units.en: I have never drunk and never cared for music, so at court gatherings no instruments are played. The ministers have seen it themselves.
units.literal: Since birth I do not drink; since birth I dislike sound—so at court informal feasts music is never played; the worthies have seen this.

units.zh: 朕三更出理事，隨事多少，事少或中前得竟，或事多至日昃方得就食。
units.en: I rise in the deep night to work. When business is light I may finish before noon. When it is heavy I eat only after the sun has slanted west.
units.literal: I rise at the third watch to handle affairs; as affairs vary—few affairs and I may finish before noon; many affairs and only at sundown may I eat.

units.zh: 日常一食，若晝若夜，無有定時。
units.en: As a rule I eat once, by day or night, at no set time.
units.literal: Usually one meal, day or night, at no fixed hour.

units.zh: 疾苦之日，或亦再食。
units.en: When I am ill I may eat twice.
units.literal: On days of illness, sometimes two meals.

units.zh: 昔要腹過於十圍，今之瘦削裁二尺餘，舊帶猶存，非爲妄說。
units.en: Once my belly measured more than ten spans around. Now I am scarcely two feet about the waist. The old belt is still here. I do not lie.
units.literal: Once my waist was more than ten girths; now I am wasted to barely two feet odd—the old belt still kept; this is no empty claim.

units.zh: 爲誰爲之？
units.en: For whom did I do this?
units.literal: For whom was it done?

units.zh: 救物故也。
units.en: For the sake of the living—that is why.
units.literal: To save the creatures—that is why.

units.zh: 《書》曰：「股肱惟人，良臣惟聖。」
units.en: The Documents say, "Arms and legs are the man; worthy ministers make the sage."
units.literal: The Documents say, "Limbs and arms are the man; good ministers make the sage."

units.zh: 向使朕有股肱，故可得中主。
units.en: Had I such ministers, I might have been a passable ruler.
units.literal: Had I such limbs and arms, I could have been a middling lord.

units.zh: 今乃不免居九品之下，「不令而行」，徒虛言耳。
units.en: As it is I remain no better than the lowest grade of ruler. "Without being ordered it is done" is only an empty phrase.
units.literal: Now I still cannot rise above the ninth grade—"without being ordered it is done" is only empty words.

units.zh: 卿今慊言，便罔知所答。
units.en: You press your case so hard that I scarcely know how to reply.
units.literal: You now speak fully—at once I do not know what to answer.

units.zh: 卿又云「百司莫不奏事，詭競求進」。
units.en: You also say, "Every office memorializes, scheming for promotion."
units.literal: You also say, "The hundred offices all memorialize, deviously competing for advancement."

units.zh: 此又是誰？
units.en: Who are they? Name them.
units.literal: Who are these again?

units.zh: 何者復是詭事？
units.en: Which are these deceptive affairs again?
units.literal: Which affairs again are the deceptive matters?

units.zh: 今不使外人呈事，於義可否？
units.en: If outsiders may no longer present memorials, is that right in principle?
units.literal: Now not to let outsiders present affairs—in principle is that permissible?

units.zh: 無人廢職，職可廢乎？
units.en: No men, no offices—can you abolish the offices themselves?
units.literal: Without men offices are abandoned—can offices be abandoned?

units.zh: 職廢則人亂，人亂則國安乎？
units.en: Abolish offices and men fall into disorder; men in disorder—and the realm is secure?
units.literal: Offices abandoned, then men are confused; men confused, then is the state at peace?

units.zh: 以咽廢飧，此之謂也。
units.en: Reject the meal because the throat hurts—that is the case.
units.literal: To reject food because of the throat—this is what is meant.

units.zh: 若斷呈事，誰屍其任？
units.en: Cut off memorials—who then answers for the charge?
units.literal: If presenting affairs is cut off, who bears the responsibility?

units.zh: 專委之人，云何可得？
units.en: Where will you find men fit to be trusted with everything alone?
units.literal: Men exclusively entrusted—how can they be obtained?

units.zh: 是故古人云：「專聽生姦，獨任成亂。」
units.en: The ancients said it plainly: "Listen to one voice and treachery is born; trust one man alone and chaos follows."
units.literal: Therefore the ancients said: "Exclusive listening breeds treachery; sole trust breeds chaos."

units.zh: 猶二世之委趙高，元後之付王莽。
units.en: Think of Er Shi handing everything to Zhao Gao, or Empress Yuan giving the realm to Wang Mang.
units.literal: Just as Er Shi entrusted Zhao Gao, and Empress Yuan entrusted Wang Mang.

units.zh: 呼鹿爲馬，卒有閻樂望夷之禍，王莽亦終移漢鼎。
units.en: Call a deer a horse, and in the end Yan Le brings ruin at Wangyi; Wang Mang too shifts the Han throne from its base.
units.literal: Calling a deer a horse—in the end came the disaster of Yan Le at Wangyi; Wang Mang also finally moved the tripod of Han.

units.zh: 卿云「吹毛求疵」，復是何人所吹之疵？
units.en: You wrote "splitting hairs for flaws"—whose flaws? Name him.
units.literal: You say "splitting hairs for flaws"—again, whose flaws are being split?

units.zh: 「擘肌分理」，復是何人乎？
units.en: "Splitting muscle to distinguish principle"—who is that?
units.literal: "Splitting muscle to distinguish principle"—again, who is it?

units.zh: 事及「深刻」「繩逐」，並復是誰？
units.en: When you speak of "severity" and "driving by the cord," who are they?
units.literal: Matters touching "severity" and "driving by the cord"—again, who are they?

units.zh: 又云「治、署、邸、肆」，何者宜除？
units.en: You also named "bureaus, offices, lodges, markets"—which should be abolished?
units.literal: You also say "administration, offices, lodges, markets"—which ought to be abolished?

units.zh: 何者宜省？
units.en: Which should be cut?
units.literal: Which ought to be reduced?

units.zh: 「國容戎備」，何者宜省？
units.en: "State ceremony and armaments"—what should be trimmed?
units.literal: "State display and military preparedness"—which ought to be reduced?

units.zh: 何者未須？
units.en: What is not needed now?
units.literal: Which are not yet needed?

units.zh: 「四方屯傳」，何者無益？
units.en: "Garrisons and relays in all four quarters"—which do no good?
units.literal: "Relay posts in all four quarters"—which are useless?

units.zh: 何者妨民？
units.en: Which harm the people?
units.literal: Which harm the people?

units.zh: 何處興造而是役民？
units.en: Where do you build at the cost of forced labor?
units.literal: Where is construction that conscripts the people?

units.zh: 何處費財而是非急？
units.en: Where is treasure spent on what is not urgent?
units.literal: Where is wealth spent on what is not urgent?

units.zh: 若爲「討召」？
units.en: What of "summons and recruitment"?
units.literal: As for "summons and recruitment"?

units.zh: 若爲「征賦」？
units.en: What of "levies and requisitions"?
units.literal: As for "levies and requisitions"?

units.zh: 朝廷從來無有此事，靜息之方復何者？
units.en: The court has never done such things. What is your plan to bring them to rest?
units.literal: The court has never had such matters from the beginning—what methods quiet and rest them?

units.zh: 宜各出其事，具以奏聞。
units.en: Let each charge be named and reported in full.
units.literal: Each should state the affair and memorialize it in full.

units.zh: 卿云「若不及于時大息其民，事至方圖，知無及也」。
units.en: You wrote, "Fail now to give the people real rest, and plan only when crisis comes—you will know you are already too late."
units.literal: You say, "If one does not at this time greatly rest the people, and only plans when the affair has arrived, one knows it will be too late."

units.zh: 如卿此言，卽時便是大役其民，是何處所？
units.en: By your own logic you are overworking the people right now—where?
units.literal: By your words, at this very moment you are greatly overworking the people—where is that?

units.zh: 卿云「國弊民疲」，誠如卿言，終須出其事，不得空作漫語。
units.en: You say "the realm is hollow and the people exhausted." If that is so, name the facts. Do not speak in empty generalities.
units.literal: You say "the state is spent and the people weary"—if it is truly as you say, in the end you must state the affairs; you cannot make empty, roaming words.

units.zh: 夫能言之，必能行之。
units.en: Who can talk must also act.
units.literal: One who can speak of it must be able to carry it out.

units.zh: 富國強兵之術，急民省役之宜，號令遠近之法，並宜具列。
units.en: Ways to enrich the state and strengthen the army, plans to spare the people and cut corvée, orders for near and far—list them all.
units.literal: Methods to enrich the state and strengthen the army, measures urgent for resting the people and reducing corvée, commands for the near and far—all should be listed in full.

units.zh: 若不具列，則是欺罔朝廷，空示頰舌。
units.en: Fail to list them and you deceive the throne with nothing but lip service.
units.literal: If you do not list them in full, then you are deceiving the court and showing only cheek and tongue.

units.zh: 凡人有爲，先須內省，惟無瑕者，可以戮人。
units.en: Before you judge others, judge yourself. Only the spotless may sit in judgment.
units.literal: Whenever a man would act, he must first look inward; only one without flaw may punish others.

units.zh: 卿不得曆詆內外，而不極言其事。
units.en: You may not slander everyone within and without the palace and still refuse to speak plainly.
units.literal: You may not go through the court inside and out with slander and not speak to the utmost of the affairs.

units.zh: 佇聞重奏，當復省覽，付之尚書，班下海內，庶亂羊永除，害馬長息，惟新之美，復見今日。
units.en: I await your next memorial. I shall read it again, send it to the Masters of Writing, and publish it throughout the realm—so the bad sheep are driven off, the harmful horse stilled, and renewal shines once more.
units.literal: I await hearing your further memorial; I shall again examine it, entrust it to the Masters of Writing, and promulgate it within the four seas—so that bad sheep may be forever removed, harmful horses long stilled, and the beauty of renewal appear again today.

units.zh: 琛奉敕，但謝過而已，不敢復有指斥。
units.en: Chen took the edict and could only apologize. He did not dare remonstrate again.
units.literal: Chen received the edict and only apologized, not daring to criticize again.

units.zh: 久之，遷太府卿。
units.en: In time he was made Minister of the Grand Treasury.
units.literal: After a long while he was transferred to Minister of the Grand Treasury.

units.zh: 太清二年，遷雲騎將軍、中軍宣城王長史。
units.en: In the second year of Taiqing he became General of the Cloud Cavalry and chief clerk to the Prince of Xuancheng, commander of the central army.
units.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he was transferred to General of the Cloud Cavalry and Chief Clerk to the Prince of Xuancheng, Commander of the Central Army.

units.zh: 侯景舉兵襲京師，王移入臺內，留琛與司馬楊曒守東府。
units.en: When Hou Jing marched on the capital the prince withdrew into the inner palace and left Chen and Marshal Yang Xun to defend the Eastern Palace.
units.literal: Hou Jing raised troops and struck the capital; the prince moved into the inner palace, leaving Chen and the marshal Yang Xun to hold the Eastern Palace.

units.zh: 賊尋攻陷城，放兵殺害，琛被槍未至死，賊求得之，轝至闕下，求見僕射王克、領軍朱异，勸開城納賊。
units.en: The rebels soon broke the city and unleashed slaughter. Chen was speared but lived. They found him, bore him in a litter to the palace gate, and demanded Wang Ke, Vice Director, and Zhu Yi, Commander of the Army, begging them to open the gates to the rebels.
units.literal: The rebels soon stormed the city, let their soldiers slaughter, and Chen was speared but not killed; the rebels found him, carried him in a litter to the palace gate, and sought audience with Vice Director Wang Ke and Commander of the Army Zhu Yi, urging them to open the city and admit the rebels.

units.zh: 克等讓之，涕泣而止，賊復轝送莊嚴寺療治之。
units.en: Wang Ke and the others reproached him until he wept and fell silent. The rebels carried him back to Zhuangyan Monastery to heal his wounds.
units.literal: Ke and the others rebuked him; weeping, he stopped, and the rebels again carried him in a litter to Zhuangyan Monastery for treatment.

units.zh: 明年，臺城不守，琛逃歸鄉里。
units.en: The next year the inner city fell. Chen fled to his home district.
units.literal: The next year the inner city could not be held; Chen fled home to his native place.

units.zh: 其年冬，賊進寇會稽，復執琛送出都，以爲金紫光祿大夫。
units.en: That winter, when the rebels marched on Kuaiji, they seized Chen again and sent him to the capital as Household Counsellor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
units.literal: That winter the rebels advanced against Kuaiji, seized Chen again, and sent him back to the capital, making him Household Counsellor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

units.zh: 後遇疾卒，年六十九。
units.en: He later fell ill and died at sixty-nine.
units.literal: Later he fell ill and died, aged sixty-nine.

units.zh: 琛所撰《三禮講疏》、《五經滯義》及諸儀法，凡百餘篇。
units.en: He wrote the Exegesis of the Three Rites, the Stalled Meanings of the Five Classics, and many works on ritual—over a hundred chapters in all.
units.literal: Chen compiled the Exegesis of the Three Rites, the Stalled Meanings of the Five Classics, and various ritual regulations—more than a hundred chapters in all.

units.zh: 子詡，太清初，自儀同西昌侯掾，出爲巴山太守，在郡遇亂卒。
units.en: His son Xu, early in Taiqing, left a post as aide to the Marquis of Xichang, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, to serve as Administrator of Bashan, and died there when rebellion swept the region.
units.literal: His son Xu, at the beginning of Taiqing, rose from aide to the Marquis of Xichang, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, and went out as Administrator of Bashan; in the commandery he met with the chaos and died.

units.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察云：夏侯勝有言曰：「士患不明經術；
units.en: Yao Cha, Chen Director of the Ministry of Personnel, said: Xiahou Sheng once said, "The scholar's trouble is not knowing the classics;
units.literal: Yao Cha, Chen Director of the Ministry of Personnel, said: Xia Hou Sheng had a saying: "The gentleman's trouble is not knowing the classics;

units.zh: 經術明，取青紫如拾地芥耳。」
units.en: Once the classics are clear, rank and office are like picking up a mustard plant from the ground."
units.literal: once the classics are clear, taking blue and purple is like picking up a mustard plant from the ground."

units.zh: 朱异、賀琛並起微賤，以經術逢時，致於貴顯，符其言矣。
units.en: Zhu Yi and He Chen both rose from humble beginnings; the classics brought them to high rank in their day—exactly as he said.
units.literal: Zhu Yi and He Chen both rose from humble beginnings; by the classics they met their time and reached noble eminence—this matched his words.

units.zh: 而异遂徼寵倖，任事居權，不能以道佐君，苟取容媚。
units.en: Yet Yi sought favor and power, held office, and could not guide his lord by the Way—only by pleasing and flattering.
units.literal: Yet Yi went on to seek favor and fortune, hold office and wield power, and could not assist his lord by the Way but only sought to please and flatter.

units.zh: 及延寇敗國，實异之由。
units.en: When the rebel ravaged the realm, the blame was truly Yi's.
units.literal: When the rebel prolonged his ravaging of the state, the fault was truly Yi's.

units.zh: 禍難旣彰，不明其罪，至於身死，寵贈猶殊。
units.en: Once disaster was plain his guilt went unnamed; even in death his honors were lavish.
units.literal: Once disaster was plain, his guilt was not made clear; even at his death, favors and gifts were still extraordinary.

units.zh: 罰旣弗加，賞亦斯濫，失於勸沮，何以爲國？
units.en: No punishment fell, rewards ran wild—how can a state encourage good and restrain evil like this?
units.literal: Punishment was not applied, reward likewise ran wild—failure in encouragement and restraint; how can such a thing be called a state?

units.zh: 君子是以知太清之亂，能無及是乎。
units.en: A gentleman therefore knows that the chaos of Taiqing could not have stopped short of this.
units.literal: The gentleman therefore knows that the chaos of Taiqing could not fail to reach this.

units.zh: 沖母，梁武帝妹新安穆公主，卒於齊世，武帝以沖偏孤，深所鍾愛。
units.en: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, a sister of Emperor Wu of Liang. She died in Qi times, and the emperor, seeing that Chong had been left partially orphaned, doted on him.
units.literal: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, sister of Emperor Wu of Liang; she died in Qi times, and the Emperor, because Chong was a lone orphan, cherished him deeply.

units.zh: 按梁武帝即位後，追尊其父為文皇帝。
units.en: After Liang Wudi's accession he honored his father posthumously as Emperor Wen.
units.literal: According to the note, after Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne he posthumously honored his father as Emperor Wen.

units.zh: 王沖傳言其母為梁武帝妹新安穆公主，與此合。
units.en: Wang Chong's biography says his mother was Liang Wudi's sister Princess Xin'an Mu, which matches.
units.literal: The biography of Wang Chong says his mother was Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess Xin'an Mu—this agrees.

units.zh: 王沖 王通弟勱 袁敬兄子樞
units.en: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu
units.literal: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu

units.zh: [2]琳，齊代娶梁武帝妹義興長公主，有子九人，嵭知名。
units.en: Lin, in Qi times, married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess of Yixing long; he had nine sons, all of whom won notice.
units.literal: Lin, in Qi times married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister Princess of Yixing long, had nine sons, and all became renowned.

units.zh: 大同末，梁武帝謁園陵，道出朱方，勱隨例迎候，队勱令從輦側，所經山川，莫不顧問，勱隨事應對，咸有故實。
units.en: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs by way of Zhufang; Mo met him as custom required. The emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; at every hill and stream he asked questions, and Mo answered each with historical precedent.
units.literal: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs; the route passed through Zhufang; Mo greeted him per custom; the Emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; every mountain and river passed, the Emperor inquired; Mo answered each matter with historical precedent.

units.zh: 尚書敬顯儁曰：「孔子云：『微管仲，吾其被發左衽矣』以此言之，右衽為是。」
units.en: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."
units.literal: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."

units.zh: 十五年，魏東益州刺史元法僧遣子景隆來拒齊師，南安太守皇甫諶及宗範逆擊之，大破魏軍於葭萌，屠十餘城，魏將丘突、王穆等皆降。
units.en: In year fifteen Wei east Yizhou inspector Yuan Faseng sent his son Jinglong against Qi; Nan'an administrator Huangfu Chen and Zongfan counterattacked, crushing the Wei army at Jiameng, sacking more than ten cities; Wei generals Qiu Tu and Wang Mu among others surrendered.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year, Wei East Yizhou Inspector Yuan Faseng sent his son Jinglong to resist Qi's army; Nan'an Administrator Huangfu Chen and Zongfan counterattacked, smashing the Wei host at Jiameng, slaughtering more than ten cities; Wei generals Qiu Tu, Wang Mu, and others all surrendered.

units.zh: 五月，封舅曼子侍中騎都尉光祿大夫王莽為新都侯。
units.en: In the fifth month, maternal uncle Man's son Wang Mang, Attendant at the Palace and Cavalry Commandant Guanglu Grandee, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xindu.
units.literal: Fifth month, enfeoffed maternal uncle Man son Attendant at the Palace Cavalry Commandant Guanglu Grandee Wang Mang as Xindu Marquis.

units.zh: 孝宣承統，纂修洪業，亦講論六藝，招選茂異，而蕭望之、梁丘賀、夏侯勝、韋玄成、嚴彭祖，尹更始以儒術進，劉向，王褒以文章顯，將相則張安世、趙充國、魏相、丙吉、於定國、杜延年，治民則黃霸、王成、龔遂、鄭弘、召信臣、韓延壽、尹翁歸、趙廣漢、嚴延年、張敞之屬，皆有功跡見述於世。
units.en: Emperor Xuan inherited the succession and carried forward the great enterprise. He too expounded the Six Arts and recruited outstanding men. Xiao Wangzhi, Liangqiu He, Xiahou Sheng, Wei Xuancheng, Yan Pengzu, and Yin Gengshi advanced through Confucian learning; Liu Xiang and Wang Bao gained distinction for their writing; among the generals and chancellors were Zhang Anshi, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Yu Dingguo, and Du Yannian; and among those who governed the people were Huang Ba, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Shao Xinchen, Han Yanshou, Yin Wengui, Zhao Guanghan, Yan Yannian, Zhang Chang, and others. All left achievements celebrated in their age.
units.literal: Emperor Xuan inherited the succession and carried forward the great enterprise. He too discussed the Six Arts and recruited outstanding men: Xiao Wangzhi, Liangqiu He, Xiahou Sheng, Wei Xuancheng, Yan Pengzu, and Yin Gengshi advanced through Confucian learning; Liu Xiang and Wang Bao gained distinction through literary composition; among the generals and chancellors were Zhang Anshi, Zhao Chongguo, Wei Xiang, Bing Ji, Yu Dingguo, and Du Yannian; among those who governed the people were Huang Ba, Wang Cheng, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Shao Xinchen, Han Yanshou, Yin Wengui, Zhao Guanghan, Yan Yannian, Zhang Chang, and others. All had achievements recounted in their age.

units.zh: 八歲，讀沈約集，見回文研銘，從典援筆擬之，便有佳致。
units.en: At eight he read Shen Yue's collected works. Seeing a palindrome study inscription, Congdian took up the brush to match it and at once produced something fine.
units.literal: At eight he read Shen Yue's collected works; seeing a palindrome study inscription, Congdian took up the brush and imitated it, and at once achieved fine effect.
